the next item on the agenda is the debate on: oral question to the council: fifteen years after beijing un platform for action on gender equality, by eva-britt svensson, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and equality (o-0006/2010 b7-0007/2010) and oral question to the commission: fifteen years after beijing un platform for action on gender equality, by eva-britt svensson, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and equality (o-0007/2010 b7-0008/2010).
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. ladies and gentlemen! we are now in the 15th anniversary of the famous world conference on women's equal rights, organized by the united nations in beijing. during this time, the 189 signatory states of the un platform for action on gender equality have managed to make some progress in all 12 areas identified in the document. however, most of the diagnoses of that time are still valid, especially those related to domestic violence against women or the participation of women in armed conflicts. these issues do not need to be brought up in the european parliament we discuss them in debates on human rights violations at almost every plenary session. i would therefore like to commend the un initiative which, every five years, carries out a detailed review of the platform for action in several hundred countries (the last one was in 2005) and identifies the most pressing issues. five years ago, at a conference in new york, the signatory states drew attention to the high rate of rape against women, the increase in hiv/aids infections among women and the discrimination against women in employment. unfortunately, the same observations could be made today. a very concrete action plan is needed, with the real support of all the signatories of the platform and the involvement of the european union, so that the next review of the programme, five years from now, will already show clear progress.
in writing. one of the twelve strategic areas defined in the beijing platform for action is women's rights as an inalienable, integral and indivisible part of universal human rights. the aim is to fully implement international instruments for the protection of these rights, including the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women. one form of discrimination is the violation of women's reproductive rights. the report on the observance of reproductive rights in poland in 2007 and the recommendations of the un human rights committee based on it clearly show that polish women have difficulty in accessing reimbursed contraception, medical care during pregnancy, prenatal examinations and even painless childbirth. they are virtually denied legal abortion even in cases where the law allows it. as a result, between 200 and 400 legal abortions are performed in poland each year, compared with 100,000 illegal ones. i propose that the legal abortion rate, calculated as the number of legal abortions per 1000 live births in a given year, be adopted as a measure of women's equality in the eu member states. in countries where women have the right to choose whether to have an abortion, the rate hovers around 200. in poland, it is 1. it is an objective measure of the violation of women's reproductive rights in poland. i call for more effective eu-un cooperation in monitoring women's rights and for the introduction of metrics to objectify violations of women's rights.
in writing. i fully share ms svensson's commitment to gender equality and agree that the issues she raises have a significant impact on the process of gender equality. at the same time, i would like to point out that many women consciously and voluntarily choose to work at home for the sake of their family. they may be forced to abandon their careers for unforeseen reasons (for example, because they have to take care of a sick or disabled child). the main problem in this case is the lack of adequate pension provision for these women. in many countries, such facilities are lacking or are unable to provide women with a decent living. it is therefore necessary to include the issue of benefits for women in household and childcare in the gender equality debate.
mr. chairman, please! i express my deep concern about the rapidly deteriorating situation of my compatriots in lithuania. lithuania is a member of the european union. nevertheless, the fundamental rights of the polish national minority are being violated in this country. almost 300,000 poles in lithuania, in areas where they make up 60-80% of the population, do not have the right to use their native language as an auxiliary in public. there's a court order to remove bilingual street signs. the bailiffs are on duty. polish names are lithuanian. they're discriminated against when the earth turns. the right of polish children to receive education in polish is curtailed. their parents' voting rights are restricted. the future of the union is at stake. do we still want to live in a europe of illusory values or of real values? it is up to us, among other things, to decide in which direction the union will go, whether we will turn a blind eye to the blatant discrimination against minorities or whether we will actually build a safe europe in the spirit of respect for human rights.
mr. chairman, please! unfortunately, once again i have to speak about the situation of the polish minority in the european union member state of lithuania. it would seem that if a country is part of the european union, it should follow all european standards. but vilnius does not. there is still no permission in this country for bilingual signs in places inhabited by the polish not so much minority as the majority. there are significant problems with the functioning of polish education. as a result of the lithuanian education authorities' actions, about 100 polish school classes will be deprived. recently, significant restrictions have been introduced for artistic groups promoting polish culture. it's a strange asymmetry, because lithuanians in poland are guaranteed all rights and a lot of funding from the polish state budget. it's time for a basic human revenge. it is time for international organisations, including our european parliament, to address the issue of discrimination against poles in lithuania.
although many economists and politicians have declared the end of the crisis in europe, we are still dealing with its negative consequences. monthly data on the unemployment rate in the union are becoming more and more depressing. more than 23 million people are now unemployed in europe. this means that the crisis has destroyed the efforts to promote employment that have been made for many years. the ever-increasing number of young people who are unemployed is a particularly damaging phenomenon. one in five young europeans is now unemployed. this situation is likely to lead to particularly harmful social consequences, such as an increase in crime, alcoholism, drug abuse and family pathologies. as regards possible ways of getting out of the recession quickly, i believe we should use our greatest asset, the community's internal market. more coordination at european level is needed to take full advantage of the potential of the common economic area. the rules of operation must be further simplified and a genuine economic union developed.
mr president, i would like to express the sorrow felt by all members of the committee on regional development at the terrible loss of life in madeira and our intention to do all we can to assist madeira in its hour of need. of course, the national and regional authorities are already doing their utmost to relieve the difficulties encountered by the people and especially those who have been left homeless and we urgently await their request for european assistance through the european solidarity fund. i am sure it will be treated with the utmost expediency by all concerned. we ask the european commission to mobilise all its resources and review with the portuguese authorities how the ongoing european programmes can be adjusted to assist the region. let me emphasise that the existing solidarity fund continues to have well-known limitations. back in april 2005 the commission adopted a proposal for the revision of the regulation, which was then adopted by the parliament at first reading in may 2006. despite the undeniable usefulness of a more flexible solidarity fund, despite the necessity of extending its ambit of operations to cover unforeseen man-made disasters and criminal acts as well as natural ones, the council has been unable to reach a common position on the review of the fund since may 2006. in the light of the terrible events in madeira we see more clearly than ever that we need a solidarity fund which could effectively meet the challenges and allow the union to deliver prompt and effective assistance when member states suffer a disaster. i would therefore call on the spanish presidency to relaunch the process of amending the solidarity fund, proving in this way that the spirit of real european solidarity remains at the heart of the european project.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has not yet adopted a position on the proposal for a directive. i thank you for the opportunity to speak to you here in parliament about the flood disaster in madeira. they have made an impressive appeal to the commission to help madeira in its present situation and to show european solidarity. the commission is prepared to do so. how exactly this can be done will have to be worked out in the next few days and weeks in close cooperation with the portuguese authorities. we must and will respect the rules of the fund. where they offer a margin of manoeuvre, the commission will use it in favour of madeira. first, the damage must be assessed, then a request for assistance must be prepared and submitted. this is the order. the regional policy dg and my colleague, commissioner hahn, will be providing advice and support. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fund's rules and regulations are properly applied. the commission made a proposal for this over four years ago, parliament gave it its support, and it is still before the council. but i would say, in a restrictive way, that the proposals we made then would not offer a better way of helping in this particular case. it is true that prevention must remain a priority of our policy. cohesion policy is the right instrument for this. i would like to reassure you that the commission will do everything in its power to help the people and the administration in madeira to cope with this terrible event.
in writing. please accept my condolences to the families of those who have died as a result of floods and landslides caused by heavy rains in madeira. nature is not to be tricked, and since we cannot prevent natural disasters, we should do everything we can to prevent their devastating effects and to help their victims. in the face of natural disasters and other crises, the european union should be able to respond quickly and efficiently, using appropriate resources. in this context, as i have already stressed in the amendments submitted to the draft report by mr danjean on the implementation of the european security strategy and the common security and defence policy, it is necessary to ensure the smooth functioning of the instruments for responding to crisis situations through well-organised command centres, respectively for pillar i and pillar ii actions. good planning and efficient management of these centres will enable successful activities to be undertaken in the member states of the european union and other countries in need. in particular, there is a need for better coordination of rescue, police, military and firefighting forces within the eu. the use of specialised trained units - such as the un-certified polish fire brigade's search and rescue (srs) team - should also be considered.
on behalf of the s&d group. european integration, security and energy solidarity require joint investment activities by all member states in energy infrastructure in the broad sense, and in particular in transmission infrastructure. optimal investment solutions in this area require objective information both on the state of infrastructure in the individual national systems and on the information necessary to carry out a central union study of their future integration. the point is that the competitiveness element in the common market for production and services, which is shaped mainly by the cost of energy in the member state concerned, and commercial secrecy should not obscure or distort integration processes. let's keep only the necessary military infrastructure secret. the main concern is that decisions on investments such as the construction of the northern and southern pipelines are not purely selfish actions in the interests of some member states of the european union. let us create a comprehensive, forward-looking energy infrastructure project for the whole union based on the principles of cooperation, trust and solidarity. unfortunately, the current regulation will only serve this purpose to a certain extent, and i believe that it should, for example, take account of the priorities of the member states.
energy and the energy grid are one of the key issues for the future of the european economy. the importance of energy security is repeated in various documents, debates and meetings. however, in order to ensure that the words and declarations are followed by concrete solutions and measurable results, it is essential to ensure that the planned investments are adequately financed. according to a report by exxon mobil, one of the world's largest oil companies, global energy demand will show a clear upward trend of 1.2% per year, increasing by about 35% by 2030. demand for gas, which will be the second most important energy source, will increase by 1.8% per year. the world now uses just over 3 trillion cubic meters . by 2030 it will need about 4.3 trillion cubic meters . the consequence of the old continent's growing demand for gas will be an increased dependence on imports of this raw material, from 45% in 2005 to 70% in 2030. in view of the above thresholds, the european community's financial support for the energy structure should be approached strategically. in the current economic and financial situation, it is particularly difficult to find investors for many projects. only with the appropriate support of the european union will it be possible to continue their implementation. priority should be given to those projects that focus on cross-border needs and contribute to the development of new technologies that are essential for europe's future energy needs. these projects will help to close the gaps in interconnections in the european union and will allow for the continued optimal exploitation of internal energy sources in the european union.
ensuring that energy supplies are uninterrupted and stable has become a priority for the governments of the member states of the union and for the community as a whole. the european commission has a particular responsibility in this respect and should, through its activities, seek to secure the energy supply of the community by developing and monitoring the proper functioning of the european energy market. one of the mechanisms of the commission's multi-dimensional energy policy should be to support efficient investment projects in the energy sector. the commission should carry out regular analyses and studies, based on information on the energy infrastructure investment projects of individual countries, with an emphasis not only on the projects currently in operation, but also on the analysis of investment projects aiming at greater diversification of both the sources of raw materials and the means of their transport and production. the commission has a coherent analysis of all the countries of the union, it will be able to choose the strategy that is most beneficial for the european energy market.
in writing. i would like to thank the rapporteur very much for producing such a balanced report. the consolidated actions of the member states and the european commission contained in it will ensure an integrated and improved energy security system for the union, while achieving better efficiency and energy savings. within the framework of the community energy policy, the commission should, together with the member states, identify the investments required to meet the eu's strategic needs for the demand and supply of natural gas and electricity. this regulation establishes a common framework under which data and information on investment projects in energy infrastructure in the oil, natural gas, electricity, biofuels and low-emission investment projects for urban heating and cooling sectors are reported to the european commission. the coal is undoubtedly an essential element for the stability of the energy system, which cannot be replaced by renewable energy sources, since they will not meet the needs of the ever-expanding and developing economic sectors of the new member states. in pointing out the advantages of coal as an energy source, it should be noted that, on the basis of the technologies developed, we can increase the reduction of pollution gradually by adapting to the set co2 emission limits.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, commissioner, i would like to thank you for your work. i would like to begin by expressing my sincere thanks to mrs patrão neves for her contribution to the preparation of this report. it takes a lot of determination and a lot of compromise to create a coherent document like this. however, this report is only a basis for the future common fisheries policy, which requires a major restructuring and fundamental changes to reconcile environmental concerns with the preservation of the historical heritage of fisheries. the essence of this policy must be regionalization, which will be based on the conditions prevailing in the individual waters. this will allow for a proper assessment based on the views of the fishing and scientific communities, and the compromise reached will ensure that fisheries operate equally and fairly. the new common fisheries policy must provide a boost to the sector in a europe in crisis, but attention must be paid to the predatory industrial fishing, particularly in the baltic sea, where healthy and valuable fish are replaced by flour fed to poultry and cattle, and toxic panga from the far east is put on europeans' tables. this is a blow to europe's coastal fisheries, which are in harmony with nature and which must be given special attention. it is also necessary to create a rational and fair fishing system to replace the rigged quota system. it is about giving equal opportunities to all fishermen in all eu countries. the ecr group supports this report in the hope that it will change the current system.
mr. chairman, please! the fisheries sector is of fundamental importance as a source of livelihood in european coastal zones and as a source of food for europe's citizens. unfortunately, the common fisheries policy in its current form fails to meet the challenges posed by a number of problems, such as uncontrolled exploitation of fisheries and overcapacity. a fundamental transformation of maritime policy is needed. we are at the beginning of a process which should lead to a genuine change in the current ineffective european fisheries policy. i thank the member for patrão neves for the comprehensive report which determines the necessary actions on which this reform should be based. first, to reduce the excessive fishing potential. this is a fundamental problem which must be addressed by the introduction of appropriate market mechanisms and their control. i'm talking about the individual quota system, or the itq. i believe that it is an economic remedy to adapt the size of the fleet to the available resources and to ensure the profitability of the fishing sector. secondly, decentralisation and the wider involvement of stakeholders and advisory bodies in this process. the aim is to increase the involvement of fishermen, to develop specific rules, which will increase trust between fishing communities and fisheries management authorities. the green paper is a good assessment of the current fisheries policy, pointing out its deep flaws. the report by mrs patrão neves analyses the possibilities for resolving the disadvantageous situation of european fisheries. however, these proposals require further discussion. otherwise, our community risks voting on another version of the reform which will not solve the problems facing european fisheries.
the common fisheries policy must reconcile ecological and environmental objectives with the size of the fisheries, as well as with employment and the living standards of fishermen's families. the fishing capacity should be adapted to the state of the stocks, the stocks being determined in accordance with the latest scientific and expert knowledge. the achievement of sustainable fishing quotas must be combined with a process of support for the fishing environment in various areas, i.e. investment, modernisation, social, and this in a multiannual perspective. the common fisheries policy should take into account the specificities of the different regions and seas. the powers of the regional advisory committees should therefore be increased and they should work closely with the fisheries administrations of the member states and the european commission. finally, it is necessary to strengthen the organisation of fishermen and to improve the chain from catching to sale, ensuring the quality and high standards of fishery products.
in writing. the green paper on the common fisheries policy leaves no stone unturned for the european commission and the member states. it is clear that not all projects and reforms within the union are successful. we should therefore draw the appropriate conclusions both at the institutional and practical level. one of the fundamental flaws of the 2002 reform was excessive centralisation. the diversity and specificity of the regions of the european union should impose a requirement for regionalisation. it is not possible for the european commission to treat the baltic sea as if it were the same as the atlantic or the mediterranean. the regionalisation of fisheries policy should be accompanied by concrete solutions to social and economic issues. from the point of view of the population living in areas dependent on fisheries, the most important direction of action is economic and social diversification and restructuring, including the creation of new jobs outside the fisheries sector. the lack of opportunities to increase catches and employment in the baltic fisheries sector should give rise to the above actions. it is a solution that fits the expectations and needs of society. research shows that two thirds of europe's fish stocks are at risk, including very popular species such as sole, plaice and cod. wwf analyses are clear: if no concrete changes are made, the mediterranean tuna breeding stock and many other species will disappear by 2012.

member of the commission. − mr president, i am very pleased that my first attendance at the plenary session of the european parliament takes place on this important day – 8 march, international women’s day. it is also an honour for me to represent the commission, and in particular vice-president reding, who will lead the commission’s efforts to protect fundamental rights. this is a unique opportunity to collectively celebrate the economic, political and social achievements of women, past, present and future. in 1957, gender equality was enshrined in the european treaties. since then, an impressive number of legal instruments, followed by a great number of decisions by the european court of justice, have created a legal arsenal at eu level. i would like to remind you that gender equality is not only a fundamental value enshrined in the treaty, but also that gender equality policies have proven to be a driver for economic growth. last friday, the president of the european commission and vice-president reding renewed the commission’s commitment to the values of gender equality by presenting a women’s charter. the women’s charter represents the political commitment of the commission to advance equality between women and men in five areas: equal economic independence; equal pay for equal work and work of equal value; equality in decision-making; dignity, integrity and an end to gender-based violence; and gender equality beyond the union. the women’s charter will be followed, in september 2010, by a new comprehensive strategy for equality between women and men. this strategy will translate the principles of the women’s charter into concrete actions to be implemented in the next five years. these are ambitious projects and objectives that the commission will not be able to achieve alone. it will need to work in close cooperation with its main partners at eu level and, in particular, with you, the european parliament and the femm committee. international women’s day is an excellent opportunity to remind us all of this commitment.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the eu directive on package holidays that we are discussing today dates back to 1990, 20 years ago, when the most popular type of holiday was a two-week package, usually booked at a travel agency and selected from the offers left in a brochure. this directive provides for basic consumer protection measures for such packages, covering in particular transparent information on offers, the right to cancel a trip, compensation for services of a lower standard and insolvency issues of travel agencies. the problem is that over the last 20 years, both the business model and the consumer behavior model have changed completely. i myself book most of my holidays online, as do many of my countrymen, and in the european union as a whole, the percentage of people who book their holidays online is already 23%. we have countries like ireland and sweden where it's as high as 40 percent, and yet almost two-thirds of those who buy their holidays this way don't realize that the protection of their interests is much lower than for people who still buy their holidays the traditional way. we should fight it. i am glad that the european commission has finally raised this issue. i think 20 years is definitely too long. i hope that we will hear from the commission today exactly when this directive will be amended and in what direction these amendments will go. it cannot be that in the european parliament or in other eu institutions we encourage eu citizens to use e-commerce services, to buy services also in cross-border trade, and at the same time we do not offer the same protection to those who do so.
i support the revision of the package travel directive, which is 20 years old and does not correspond to the current realities. today, more than half of consumers are making their own travel arrangements, often using the internet and low-cost airlines. my predecessors have spoken of it. however, not all have pointed out that the scope of the directive should be clearly defined. it can't be that you don't know what it's about. this is not good for consumers or good for business. i think it is unnecessary to extend the scope of the directive to individual products or packages purchased from different suppliers. the extension of the requirements of the directive to dynamic affiliate sales packages would ultimately be paid for by the consumer in the form of a more expensive ticket. i cannot imagine, for example, that a hotel purchased by clicking on wizz hotels immediately after the purchase of a wizzair ticket would constitute a package subject to the requirements of the directive. the consumer needs to know whether and to what extent he is protected by eu law in the case of a particular journey. everything else is a free market thing. it would be a good idea to designate the journeys covered by the directive with a special pan-european logo.
member of the commission. - mr president, i would first of all like to thank and commend the work done by the two rapporteurs, mr lehne, who has just spoken, and mr sterckx. as president lehne has said, i would like to point out that this commission proposal for a directive is in response to a request from the european parliament. the parliament's resolution is dated 18 december 2008. it had called on the commission to submit a legislative proposal to enable member states to exclude micro-entities from the scope of the accounting directives. at the same time, the high level group on reducing administrative burdens, chaired by mr stoiber - as you have just said, mr lehne - has clearly expressed its support for this proposal. finally, the european economic and social committee has supported this proposal for simplification of accounting. so here we are. why is this measure important? the proposal is intended to enable member states to harmonise, to make more consistent, the reporting requirements of all micro-entities by creating a single reporting system. this new approach should lead to significant cost reductions for these entities. mr. lehne, you said several billion. i have the figures from my services, which, in the upper range, estimate these savings at 6.3 billion euros. even if this figure were less, i think it would justify the end of the debate on this subject, in order to encourage the activity of european micro-entities. that is also why i am calling for the proposal on these micro-entities to be adopted quickly. if this proposal were to be included in a more general framework, that of the revision of the accounting directives, as was desired - i have noted this - by the committee on economic and monetary affairs, it would certainly take more time, or even several years, before the provisions would be applicable. at the moment, ladies and gentlemen, i am hearing criticisms, remarks and proposals from both sides and i would like to try to answer or reassure on three particular points. firstly, what the proposal does is to give member states an option which they can choose to exercise or not exercise, i.e. member states which wish to do so can maintain the current rules without having to amend their own national regulations. secondly, i would like to stress that this proposal is in the direction of simplification and subsidiarity. in order for citizens and businesses to understand the internal market, to take ownership of it, we must not impose rules at european level when they are not really necessary. i think that in the specific context of micro-entities, the current rules may seem excessive. thirdly, contrary to what has been said, this proposal does not necessarily mean that accounting requirements for micro-entities should be abolished. i know that was a fear expressed in some states. the compromise proposed by the committee on legal affairs is quite clear on this point. these companies will have to keep supporting documents which give a concrete picture of the transactions carried out and their own financial situation. in conclusion to these few introductory words and before i listen to you, i want to personally encourage parliament to support this proposal. the parties involved are waiting for this decision and i think a strong signal from parliament is needed to move this matter forward now. we are all in favour of simplification. i think that this proposal which president lehne is very keenly supporting is an example of this simplification and i hope that micro-entities will soon be able to benefit from the savings which are expected from this proposal.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. we are well aware of the differences between microenterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises, let alone between microenterprises and large economic bodies. i would therefore like to draw attention to the negative environmental factors for the activities of these companies. these are both macro factors, such as legislation, taxes and red tape, and micro factors, such as difficulties with excess, low liquidity. what is the cause of this situation? well, it's causing the first-year survival rate of micro-enterprises to hover around 60 percent for the last few years. this means that more than one third of newly created micro-enterprises did not survive their first year on the market. if we also consider that in many member states micro-enterprises represent more than 90% of all economic operators, the discussion on reducing administrative barriers and burdens of various kinds, especially those related to accounting, becomes absolutely necessary. it is also important that discussions focus not only on simplification but also on the significance of financial reporting requirements for such small operators. the debate on simplification is generally focused on costs, while the debate on the meaning of requirements is about the benefits of financial reporting and the individual users and their needs. there are several features that distinguish microenterprises from large enterprises that make it advisable to introduce simplified regulations for microenterprises. first, the benefits of implementing global standards are certainly less than for large companies. this leads to a mismatch between the benefits and costs of applying standards. the appropriate cost-benefit relationship requires cost containment. secondly, financial reporting does not play a significant role in meeting the information needs of micro-enterprise owners these are usually family members. when we talk about the need for change in the wake of the financial crisis, let's remember that it wasn't micro-enterprises that caused the crisis.
in writing. i am very pleased that we are reducing the bureaucratic burden on companies by adopting new reporting rules for micro-enterprises. the fact that dozens of regulations are hampering people's entrepreneurship is one reason why the lisbon strategy has not been able to achieve its objectives. in particular, bureaucratic constraints affect small and medium-sized enterprises, for which accounting and legal costs are disproportionate to their revenues. how can the eu be the most competitive economy in the world if companies are subject to so many regulations? it is a shame to say that too many regulations that are embarrassing to businesses are authored by brussels, thus contributing to further restrictions on economic freedom. the commission's initiative was therefore fully deserving of support, even if the legal affairs committee's amendments were adopted. it is not useful to maintain complex reporting rules for small enterprises. if the eu is to develop at the pace we all want, we must take further steps to remove unnecessary obstacles. i therefore call on the european commission to complement the eu 2020 strategy with a clear objective of reducing the number of eu rules that hinder entrepreneurship. it is urgent to identify areas that are unnecessarily regulated and to eliminate such regulation. otherwise, europe will remain the region that develops more slowly than the other advanced economies in the world.
the rapporteur. - i am pleased to present the 19th internal market scoreboard presented last july. this document shows that member states are doing better at implementing eu law. once again, the objective set by the heads of state or government of keeping the average implementation deficit below 1% has been achieved. but the number of directives that have not yet been implemented in one or more member states, i.e. the fragmentation of the market, is still too high. this is over 100 internal market directives. in addition, as many as 22 directives have not been implemented for another 2 years after the deadline for transposition. member states must do even more to make the internal market a source of benefit for all europeans. as i present this report to you, i have another scoreboard in my hands, the 20th anniversary edition, which shows further progress in the implementation of eu legislation. the transposition deficit is falling to 0.7%, well below the target. that's the best score in history. it is clear that the work of the european commission, which has resulted in this publication, has a mobilizing effect on the member states. the commission can be congratulated on this good, hard work. the other good news is that market fragmentation is going down from 6% to 5%. however, 74 directives remain unimplemented in one or more eu countries, which keeps barriers, very harmful barriers, within the internal market for citizens and businesses. we have to break down these barriers together. to this end, the report by the internal market committee proposes closer cooperation between all those who share responsibility for implementing eu legislation and those who benefit from the common market. we propose to organise an annual single market forum simfo, which would bring together the european institutions, but also the member states, national parliamentarians and business and consumer representatives. the forum will provide an opportunity to exchange experience and best practice in the implementation of union law and to prepare strategies to meet the challenges that still lie ahead. to remove these harmful barriers, we call on the european commission to apply the internal market test to any new eu legislation to ensure that it does not adversely affect the freedoms that the european union has developed. it is also very the rapporteur. - first of all, i would like to thank you very much for this fascinating debate, for the lively reactions, for the serious reflections, and the presence and speeches of both commissioners and the numerous commission staff gathered show that this new parliament and this new commission will work well and closely together to further develop the common market. the single market is one of the greatest achievements of the european union and i thank you very much for the positive response to the proposals i made in my report. and to my socialist colleagues who are afraid of paragraph 10 - in writing. a society that is free to exploit the opportunities offered by the single market is the key to the success of the european integration process. we cannot build a true, united union without convincing people that all of europe is their home. and that is what solvit can do first and foremost. it is safe to say that the creation of solvit in 2002 was one of those events in the history of a united europe that may seem unremarkable on the surface, but over time brings unexpected consequences. the idea of this system goes straight to the roots of european integration, namely that it is meant to serve the citizens of the union first and foremost, not individual countries or governments. what could be better than giving ordinary people a simple tool to solve problems that limit their freedom to function within the single market? however, experience gained over the last decade has shown that there are many barriers to taking full advantage of the opportunities offered by the system. the report prepared by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection should therefore be endorsed. the main focus should be on promoting solvit among the citizens of the member states, as knowledge of it is limited. the allocation of more financial and human resources, additional training of staff or the creation of a liaison officer institution will not make sense if people do not know that they have such an instrument at their disposal. i think that this is the starting point for all action, without abandoning the others.

in writing. - consumer protection is a very important issue for the commission to address. of course, effective action alone will not be enough if consumers do not get involved. consumers must be aware of their rights. making the most of the opportunities offered by the single european market is a major challenge for the commission. to meet this challenge, effective consumer protection must be one of the eu's priorities. i believe that the use of scoreboards for consumer markets, as one of the tools for monitoring markets, is most beneficial from the consumer's point of view. these tables clearly indicate which markets do not sufficiently respond to consumer needs. analysis of these indicators shows, inter alia, that consumers face particular problems in the services market and that cross-border online trade between member states is largely organised by cross-border barriers. i'm pleased to say that there are plans for more boards. i also hope that they will provide even more detailed information than the previous ones. such tools make it much easier to understand consumer problems and respond to their needs. there is no doubt that the introduction of eu consumer protection legislation in individual eu countries is beneficial for our citizens.
in writing. − competition policy is one of the main and earliest agreed community policies. the justification and necessity of such a procedure is directly linked to one of the main objectives of the european communities, namely the creation of a common market for the member states. competition policy is designed to ensure that barriers to internal trade within the common market are not replaced by other actions by firms or governments that distort competition. competition policy is primarily concerned with the interests of consumers and seeks to ensure that they have easy access to goods and services offered in the single market at prices that are as close as possible to each other. i would simply like to draw your attention to the serious crisis that has struck europe and to say that a well-functioning internal market is the key to a healthy economy and certainly to the recovery that awaits us in the near future.
in writing. − europe, hit by the economic crisis, was able to react quickly and mitigate the effects of the crisis thanks to a common currency, a strong internal market and a stable social protection system. it's not that there aren't any repercussions, but there are signs of improvement. unfortunately, consumers still face problems in taking advantage of competition. their rights must be protected and their awareness and knowledge increased. the proper functioning and competitiveness of the european market gives consumers the opportunity to benefit from the competitive system through the choice of products, services and lower prices. however, insufficient competition is a current phenomenon, particularly in the pharmaceutical and telecommunications sectors. the lack of competition is directly harmful to consumers as well as to the economy. there is also a need to monitor competitive behaviour on the union fuel markets. in order to ensure the effective enforcement of competition law, the commission should be able to impose fines on undertakings that infringe competition law. above all, however, the crisis has exposed the weaknesses of the european economy and highlighted areas that need to be strengthened. furthermore, all economic policy strategies must be subject to democratic control and implemented with due regard for the well-being and respect for the rights of european citizens.
in writing. − the internal market scoreboard is a very important tool for informing the member states on the state of implementation of european legislation. despite their obligations, member states are either late in implementing the law in time or are introducing the rules incorrectly. the table shows that member states are improving their implementation, but a large group of countries still fall short of the target. we need a clear commitment from the member states to improve these indicators. we have been talking a lot lately in the european parliament about the need to deepen the internal market. however, the internal market will not function properly if the rules that are the basis for a well-functioning internal market are not implemented correctly and in a timely manner. the internal market must also be supported by our citizens. i therefore support the rapporteur's initiative to organise an annual internal market forum and the 'internal market test', which is an initiative to test legislation against the four freedoms of the internal market: the movement of capital, goods, services and people.

in writing. the problem of the proper functioning of the railway market in the new member states, and thus a factor limiting market liberalisation, is the inadequate financing of the railways, i.e. the lack of sufficient funds to maintain the railway infrastructure (resulting in high rates of access to it and consequently limiting the competitiveness of this transport sector due to the high transport costs), and the under-financing of public service activities, which results in the indebtedness of the passenger transport companies providing these services while limiting investment possibilities, for example, for new rolling stock. in the context of proper regulation of the european railway market, there is a need to strengthen national market regulators. by empowerment i mean increasing their independence, efficiency, staffing levels, etc. it also seems essential to establish a european market regulator to monitor the proper performance of the functions assigned to national regulators and to report on irregularities directly to the european commission.
in writing. dear members, the acta (anti-counterfeiting trade agreement) currently being negotiated by the european commission goes beyond the principle of proportionality, which states that the union's action does not go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaty. the chapter on the internet is particularly worrying. the agreement reportedly contains provisions that could restrict freedom of expression on the one hand and commercial activity on the internet on the other. this would reportedly include the introduction of liability for content uploaded by internet providers and criminal penalties for downloading files for private use. i use the word 'similarly' because the information on the contract is not from official sources but only from rumours and leaks, and the commission does not keep parliament informed of the progress of the negotiations. the treaty of lisbon already provides for such a procedure. moreover, parliament's consent, expressed by a majority of its votes, is necessary for the council to reach an agreement. the new treaty also introduces a competence to take measures in the field of intellectual property, which falls equally to the parliament and the council. i therefore join the voice of meps who are calling for more transparency in the negotiations and believe that interinstitutional cooperation on acta should confirm that all the institutions are taking the new treaty seriously. not yet, it's not.

in writing. i would like to make a few comments on the european security strategy and the common security and defence policy. the european parliament's draft resolution correctly defines the main threats and challenges facing europe. the problem is that we can't answer them well enough, or at least not always quickly enough. there are three main weaknesses, the overcoming of which would radically improve the effectiveness of the common security and defence policy. the first weakness is the lack of determination on the part of all the countries making up the european union to pursue a common policy, rather than merely declaring its need. secondly, there is a lack of coordination between the various european institutions. there is no crisis response centre at union level. finally, and thirdly, the military and civilian capabilities of the union, and not just those of individual states, are too small. air transport problems, for example, are already commonplace, and this is essential for rapid response in emergency situations. only progress in these three areas would improve the effectiveness of the common security and defence policy.
the european union clearly needs a new strategy to help and shape our response to the economic and financial crisis. an important element of the strategy should be to strengthen the free movement of people, and this applies to all groups: workers, entrepreneurs, scientists, students and even pensioners, and this is enshrined in our resolution. it is also good to put more emphasis on supporting small and medium-sized enterprises. without the development of such companies, the situation in the union will not improve. some people think that the strategy does not mention cohesion policy enough. i do not know if that is the case, because we do have a record of this fundamental importance of cohesion policy for the future of the union. but i know that if it's not implemented, then no strategy will make it better.
the new eu strategy is in fact the younger brother of the lisbon strategy. if he follows the example of his older brother, he will fail the exam and even fail to finish his university studies. at the same time that the leaders of the european union were talking about the need to adopt the lisbon strategy, in reality the member states were restricting the free movement of workers and services. the new strategy is obviously a little bit better than the version of a few months ago, where there was no mention of consistency at all. but it's more of a wish concert for now. we will review this strategy in the seven-year budget of the european union from 2014. i hope that this will be a strategy that does not serve the domination of the new european union by the countries of the old union.

madam president! the resolution presented here illustrates very well the superiority of climate policy over energy security in the european union. it also reflects well the anti-nuclear prejudices of some in this room. nuclear energy, as it happens, is the only commercially proven low-carbon energy source, yet it is subjected to very strong criticism in this resolution. the european union's limited financial resources are to be invested in selected energy sources, simply because they are renewable, interfering very strongly with the market. such a policy will certainly reduce the expenditure needed today for strategic major infrastructure projects or support for interconnectors. that money will simply not be enough for energy security. that is why we cannot support this resolution today.
the debate on investing in low-carbon technologies is a debate on how member states' economies can adapt to the conditions of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. although the climatic and weather conditions of the last few months on our continent not only give arguments to those scientists who question the human influence on climate change through co2 emissions, when we talk about low-carbon technologies, the question must be asked in this context: how to provide the necessary resources for the development of clean technologies to achieve maximum effects in the shortest possible time? i believe that the system of support for research and development should be as flexible as possible in order to allow the management of resources in line with the dynamics of scientific research. the question is whether and how appropriate mechanisms are to be set up to support investment in low-carbon technologies. finally, i would also like to add that while there are some strong arguments for investing in the development of low-carbon technologies, this should not be at the expense of cohesion policy.
madam president! the commission communication of 23 january 2008 entitled 'supporting early demonstration activities in the field of sustainable energy from fossil fuels' as part of the climate and energy package stated that the european union would support the construction of 10 to 12 ccs demonstration units. at the end of 2008, the european parliament also addressed this issue in a resolution. point 11 of that document stated that the measures presented by the commission were insufficient to provide the desired incentives to set up at least 12 demonstration plants by 2015. however, in paragraph 18 it was considered absolutely necessary that at least 12 demonstration installations for which support is envisaged should include possible combinations of 3 ccs technologies. the financing should instead come from the sale of 300 million co2 allowances under the new entrants reserve, the so-called ner300. the amount of support for the construction of demonstration plants will therefore depend on the market price of the allowances. it is estimated to be between 7 and 12 billion euros. the proposed commission decision on this project shows that the ner300 support will cover 6 ccs projects in the energy sector and 2 in industry. does the council, in agreement with the commission, intend to support the construction of a further 2 to 4 units, and if so, how?
one of the key priorities of the european union's long-term strategy should be to create an innovative economy, including by transforming the current energy system, based on a low-carbon model, in particular on clean coal technologies. the eu's primary energy supply is still about 80% fossil fuel. in the last decades, networks, supply chains have been improved to supply society with energy from these sources. economic growth and prosperity have been built on oil, coal and gas, so it's hard to change that overnight. the european strategic energy technology plan, which is a pillar of the european union's energy and climate policy, is a good step towards making the european union an innovation economy, provided, of course, that it takes into account the financing of clean coal technologies. if europe is to achieve ambitious reduction targets in a cost-effective way, it is essential to increase research expenditure on clean, sustainable and efficient energy technologies, and to coordinate the pooling of public and private sector strengths, potential and resources. industrial revolutions in the past have shown that technology can permanently change the way we live. we now have a unique and real opportunity to change the patterns of energy production. however, investment in the development and promotion of clean, renewable energy sources can only be realised if the community provides the appropriate level of funding and includes such investment in the list of strategic objectives of the european union.
in writing. global warming caused by human activity is a fact. countering this process and its negative effects is the need of the hour. the way to deal with these problems is clean, renewable energy. however, in order for them to play a significant role in the european energy system, two conditions must be met. first, to increase funding for research into their development. secondly, increase funding for investments implementing cutting-edge low-emission technologies. investing in the development of low-carbon technologies as part of the epste plan is important from an eu-wide perspective. however, it is particularly important for countries whose energy sector for historical reasons emits large amounts of co2. one such country is poland. the improvement and development of carbon capture and storage (css) technology is vital for the entire polish economy.

the author. - the mexican authorities, including president felipe calderón, have been waging a bloody war against drug gangs for several years. they had over 40,000 soldiers in the war and had some successes. these successes have undoubtedly included the arrest of the bosses of the sinaloa and juarez cartels, the destruction of over 23,000 hectares of opium crops, 38,000 hectares of marijuana, the closure of over 50 illegal drug laboratories and the arrest of over 45,000 people involved in the process. we must be aware that the mexican drug cartels bring in billions of dollars a year, far more than the government spends on the drug problem. so gangs spend vast sums to bribe politicians, judges, and police officers. that's why the government is losing this war. since 2006, nearly 15,000 people have been killed, including more than 6,000 in october last year alone. journalists are particularly at risk, with more than 60 journalists killed, most recently jorge ochoa martínez. we have to realize that without international involvement, mexico will not win this war. on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. at a time when a growing number of countries are moving away from the death penalty, the decision of the constitutional court of south korea should be received with surprise at the very least. the death penalty is a clear violation of human rights, because human life is a value that should be protected by law, and a legal system that allows the death penalty is fundamentally wrong and hypocritical. there are many arguments against this approach to justice. the most important thing to me is that it's irreversible. the death penalty is the ultimate punishment. it takes away the one, the greatest thing a person will ever have. moreover, the moral responsibility rests with the perpetrators of this act, because there is always the risk of executing an innocent person. the constitutional court's verdict is further disappointing because we know that no executions have been carried out in korea for years. i hope this decision doesn't affect the number of sentences. furthermore, i call for a complete end to the death penalty in this country.
on behalf of the s&d group. south korea is one of the european union's key trading partners. it is also the country with which the european commission has concluded negotiations for a free trade agreement, giving both parties very wide access to their markets. with such close economic ties, i am surprised that the eu and korea are so far apart in respect for human rights. all member states of the union are signatories to protocol no 13 to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, which prohibits the use of the death penalty. moreover, the union has declared its intention to work towards the universal abolition of the death penalty at international level. the union should express its strong support for the movement to abolish the death penalty in korea, according to that declaration. we hope that a moratorium on its implementation will be introduced as a first step and that the korean government will actively participate in the work to abolish the death penalty, carried out in the un forum. as the european parliament, under the new powers in the field of trade policy, we have the right and the duty to demand the abolition of the death penalty in all the european union's partner countries.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. if the views on the death penalty as they are today had been held in europe during the time of the nuremberg trials, none of the nazi criminals who were tried by that tribunal and who were responsible for the cruel death of millions of innocent people would have been sentenced to death. i have not heard of anyone in europe who has criticized the unjust decisions of the nuremberg tribunal. europe is moving further and further away from the essence of just punishment, which is a response proportionate to the evil done by the perpetrator and the guilt he bears. when we talk about murder, the killing of many people, for example in a terrorist act, or the genocide of millions of people, which happened in europe as well, the question of proportional punishment arises. the fact is that in europe too, there is an ongoing debate in scientific circles about the effectiveness of this punishment in terms of its preventive effect and the protection of innocent human lives. but that's not the key argument here. europe has now abandoned the death penalty, it is a democratic choice, we want it to be respected. but we also have to respect the choices of others, and that's why i'm all for talking about this, including talking to people in south korea. this is a democratic state, a democratic country.
i think we should not comment on this matter, we should not interfere in this matter for at least two reasons. firstly, because south korea is a democratic country and the constitutional court's ruling is a ruling of the legal authority of the country. so there is no danger that this punishment will be imposed on political or non-essential issues it will be imposed on criminals and murderers. second, the death penalty is a deterrent. of course, there's no empirical way to prove this, but if we assume the syllogism is true, that the harshest punishment is the most deterrent, that means the harshest punishment is the most deterrent, and that means the death penalty is the most deterrent. so, by using the death penalty, we are actually saving the lives of innocent people. the european union and the european parliament should therefore not interfere with the south korean authorities in this matter.
mr. chairman, please! it is with sadness that we must accept the decision of the constitutional court of south korea on the constitutionality of the death penalty. the decision is a step backwards in the country's decade-long moratorium on the death penalty. the last execution was 13 years ago. there are currently 57 inmates on death row awaiting execution. we have to be critical of the south korean court's decision. as the economic leader of the region, it should set an example in respecting the right to life of every individual. the death penalty is not compatible with the modern criminal justice system and contrary to popular belief, it does not lead to a decrease in crime.
i would like to point out that the decision of the constitutional court in south korea is disappointing and disturbing. although the last execution in the country was in 1997, the tribunal ruled on february 25 that the death penalty is a form of punishment that does not violate the constitutional right to life. this is the second judgment of the tribunal on the same subject. the first ruling was in 1996, when the tribunal also found that there was no social climate for the abolition of the death penalty. so it can be concluded that this climate is still not there, and it is a pity, because the country that is the economic leader should be an example for other countries in respecting the basic human right, which is the right to life. acting president of the council. - mr president, in these early months of 2010 we are witnessing an extraordinarily strong dynamic in the european union, in the midst of the most serious economic crisis we have known for 80 years and, at the same time, we are launching a new treaty, the treaty of lisbon, setting up new institutions and making a very extensive reorganisation of the regulation of our economic systems. it is occurring in a sometimes disorderly way, responding to major challenges on the move - for example, at the moment, the situation of the greek financial system - but europe is responding to this situation by creating new economic policy instruments in all dimensions. so sometimes trees don't let us see the forest, but a whole new way of approaching the very complex economy of the 21st century is being created and it is being done with a european approach. this has been done when the very serious crisis has been responded to and there has been an immediate reaction of injection of public money into the economies which has produced large deficits. this has been done by tackling - and we are here in the european parliament to decide on this - a whole reform of the supervision of the financial system. this is being done by addressing the coordination of economic policies, and the commission has indicated that it will present a proposal to that effect, for the coordination of economic policies, essentially within the euro area. and we are also seeing very determined, very clear action by the european union to support the financial stability of the euro area: a political commitment adopted on 11 february to consolidate and maintain the financial stability of the euro area. within this set of actions there is certainly one more: the commitment to a new strategy for growth and the creation of quality jobs, which is the central theme of this weekend's european council; a strategy which has been expressed and developed by the european commission in the document of 3 march and which will be studied mainly by the heads of state and government at the spring council, mainly from the perspective of the so-called 'strategic objectives', the strategic objectives which the european commission has identified in its document, such as the issues of employment, investment in research and development, climate change and energy, school dropout, education in general and poverty. the european council will also address the issue of governance, which we consider to be one of the shortcomings of the so-called lisbon strategy, a governance which is intended to be based on the presence of the political leadership of the european council and the action of the commission in monitoring the compliance of the states with the commitments they have themselves made, with the close cooperation and control of all this by the european parliament and all the institutions of the union, of course. that will be the main objective of the european council meetings this weekend, to which will be added an important section, the one on the fight against climate change, where the union's leadership is maintained. the european union maintains its global leadership in the fight against climate change; it must do so, it must continue to maintain that leadership. and there's a quantified commitment in the so-called "fast start". we hope, therefore, that the european council will quantify and reaffirm this commitment in the years ahead to help developing countries also tackle the fight against climate change; and a commitment by the developed countries in general to work with those that are not yet developed and to ensure that we all arrive in the best possible conditions at the all-important cancún conference, where the european union must maintain - i repeat - the leadership it has at present, without which the copenhagen agreements, which we consider insufficient, would certainly not have been achieved. the european union has reaffirmed, at 27, its full support for these objectives and its desire for clear progress towards legally binding commitments at the cancun conference in mexico. these are essentially the issues which the heads of state or government will be discussing. it is also possible, depending on what is happening at this very moment, when the whole of the european institutions are discussing how to deal with the crisis of the so-called greek case, that they will deal with the issue of the financial situation in greece and the refinancing of the public debt in greece. that issue will also undoubtedly be there, because it is part of a political commitment that the european union adopted at the level of heads of state and government on 11 february, a political commitment to support the financial stability of the euro area, in the sense that if it is necessary to take concrete measures to maintain that financial stability, those measures will be taken. that is, in any case, the principle which will be very much in evidence at this weekend's european council meeting.
president of the commission. − mr president, it is indeed a very good and timely opportunity for us to meet today – one day before the important spring european council. we have challenging tasks ahead of us. for those tasks, the fresh and forceful backing of the european parliament is of great importance. having said this, i want to thank and congratulate parliament for its resolution on europe 2020, which it adopted in strasbourg two weeks ago with broad party support. i also want to take the opportunity to thank the spanish presidency of the council for its support for the europe 2020 strategy. that support was clearly expressed at different formations of the council of ministers. but now to the european council: i believe every european council must do two things. it must show that it is responding to the needs of the moment, and it must work on europe’s long-term strategic framework and long-term strategic objectives. the crisis entails several pressing concerns for communities, workers and businesses across europe. and, as we know, public finances at national level are under unprecedented strain. the european union must of course tackle these issues, including financial stability. (i will come back to this again later.) europe must not make the mistake of neglecting the imperative of working now to bring about long-term change. that is why the european council will deal with two of our most obvious long-term challenges: our economic future, and climate change. we have already debated the europe 2020 strategy together in this parliament. your contribution and your commitment will be indispensible in carrying through our ambitions for smart, sustainable, inclusive growth. so, too, will be the contribution of the european council. our level of ambition must be set by the scale of the tasks ahead. we need to show that we have the vision and the coherence to act. and we must be able to communicate this, to show people that our actions will make a difference where it matters. this is why i believe it is so important that the european council agrees clear targets this week. the targets which the commission has put on the table were carefully chosen. they address the need to increase the level of employment, to invest more in research and innovation, to meet our 2020 climate and energy targets, to improve our educational performance and to combat poverty. these five headline targets pinpoint objectives which people can relate to, and show that the european union is leveraging reform in areas that everybody knows are important. this is also about the political will to tackle tough problems. of course the targets must be achievable. they should also require an extra effort compared to the status quo, a recognition by our member states that change is needed, and i will try to convey to the european council this sense of urgency for the economic situation of europe now and for the need of reforms for a more sustainable, more inclusive economy and society in europe. what is really important is the measures which each member state will take to boost its growth rate and address the shortcomings we all know are there. we need national measures to address national problems defined according to national circumstances and in full respect of subsidiarity, but set within a common european framework. (if there is a lesson from the financial crisis, it is that we are all interdependent in the world. so we cannot accept the principles of interdependence globally and reject them when discussed at european level.) a common framework, too, which is supported and should be stimulated by particular european union measures, what we call in our document ‘flagship initiatives’. these flagship proposals will show the european union level acting in critically important areas such as the digital agenda, innovation, resource efficiency and industrial policy – and of course in some cases, will also help targets to be achieved at a national level. what we are proposing here is a new departure. thanks to the lisbon treaty we can go for a new approach to economic coordination, a reinforced economic governance of europe – one which gives the freedom necessary to target at the national level, but which brings a strong european dimension, and using all the instruments at european level to kick-start the economy. accepting this approach will be the real test for the european council. i am encouraged by the results of the informal european council. i hope that the european leaders will be present and say ‘yes’ when it comes to responding to these challenges in a collective spirit. regarding climate change, i know that this parliament shares my conviction that climate change is not a subject that can be put on the back burner. we need to keep this top of our agenda. the european union has been in the lead, and we still are – we alone have the reduction commitments clearly backed up with the mechanisms to deliver; we are the number one donors of aid to developing countries on climate issues. so let us move on from soul-searching about copenhagen and take the initiative once again. we need a clear, unified and ambitious position. that is why the commission has put forward a communication setting out the steps needed to reinvigorate international negotiations. at the same time commissioner hedegaard has started a set of consultations with our key partners. so we should make a serious effort to advance at cancún – building on the very real substance of the copenhagen accord. we should keep kyoto on the agenda, but make clear that it can only be assessed in the light of a global agreement and not before. we should step up outreach activities and build trust, most obviously with developing countries – which is why respecting our pledges on fast-start finance is so important. and of course, at the same time, we will continue to implement our 20-20-20 package, showing in particular how it is compatible with the work of economic modernisation and reform set out in the 2020 strategy. these two areas show vividly how europeans are looking to the european union’s political leadership for action. i am convinced that, if we have the will to be bold, we can show europe as the decisive influence in building the right future for our citizens. it is in the same spirit that i will present to the european council some of the major challenges for the g20 that will take place in june in canada. in fact we should never forget that some of those issues are european but they should also be addressed at global level. financial stability and the economic and financial situation in greece are not on the formal agenda of this european council. however, frankly speaking, i cannot see how it is possible for heads of state and government, notably those in the euro area, not to discuss this issue. let me therefore state our position on this. greece is currently in the process of correcting its government excessive deficit. bringing the deficit down vigorously is crucial and greece has been taking measures to that effect. in particular, greece is taking measures leading to a reduction of its deficit this year by 4% of the gdp. such fiscal effort is in line with the course of action recommended by the commission and the council, as acknowledged by the council on 16 march. naturally, greece’s fiscal effort must be continued, it is the only way to secure a lasting reduction in the cost of debt financing.in response to the economic and financial situation in greece, the informal meeting of the heads of state or government on 11 february stated that, and i quote, ‘euro-area member states will take determined and coordinated action, if needed, to safeguard financial stability in the euro area as a whole’. the commission believes it is now appropriate to create, within the euro area, an instrument for coordinated action which could be used to provide assistance to greece in case of need. it should be clear that the creation of such a mechanism will not imply its automatic activation. creating such a mechanism is also a question of responsibility and solidarity. solidarity is a two-way street. greece is making an economic effort at this point and by supporting this effort, we not only help greece, but the stability of the eurozone as a whole. the framework for coordinated action should be understood as a safety net to be used only when all other means to avoid a crisis have been exhausted, including first and foremost exhausting the scope for policy action at domestic level. beyond technical aspects, any possible solution must reinforce and strengthen the unity and the coherence of the eurozone and its governance. the world economy needs stability. the eurozone is a pole of stability, and it is important that its capacity to provide stability is further enhanced. we may need to resort to intergovernmental instruments for some issues, but they need to be embedded into a joint european framework. it is my firm conviction that the response to the specific challenges will also be a test to european leaders and to their commitment to the european – and monetary – union. what is at stake is the essential principle of financial stability that is central to the euro; and the euro is one of the most important creations of the european project and the european construction process so far. i hope this issue will be solved in a spirit of responsibility and solidarity. that is the european way to do it. (applause)
