be looking for remedies to the crisis we are in today that will only make things worse. i do not think that more bureaucratization, integration and regulation in europe can help what is and should be our main objective, namely to increase competitiveness. we should not rely on officials to decide for free enterprise how to make our continent better. we should also respect the differences in economic and social policies that divide european countries, which are the result of their different histories, cultures, different circumstances. we can and should appeal for european solidarity with greece and i hope that words of appreciation for the greek government will come from this chamber.
instead of discussing the implementation of the europe 2020 agenda, i propose that we focus on what we are really influencing. we certainly have the influence to protect the common market from protectionism. we are certainly making european law easier for businesses, so that it does not restrict the competitiveness of the european economy. better legislation is a particular responsibility of this house, this parliament. countries will reform if they are subjected to the pressures of the global economy. that is why it is so important that we leave the member states the maximum freedom in the competitiveness of their tax, social and economic systems. by harmonizing these areas, we are only preserving the pathology of the european social model. it is freedom, not another strategy, that is the right response to the crisis.
madam president! the european council, which is preparing to define the union's new economic strategy, must draw lessons from the failure of the lisbon strategy and look at all member states in a spirit of solidarity and fairness. to be able to compete on global markets, we need to be innovative, but diverting the bulk of budgetary resources to this purpose alone will de facto discriminate against many central and eastern european countries, including poland. there is a great deal of expectation that eu funding will help spain, portugal and other eu countries develop their airport, road, rail and internet infrastructure. the eastern border regions of the european union, such as the lublin region, should be given particular priority and a special budget line should be created for them under the 2020 strategy. the council summit cannot send the signal that it is the poor regions of the union that will finance ideas whose benefits will be maximised only in the old member states.
in writing. the european council meeting starting tomorrow will focus on the general framework of the eu's new europe 2020 strategy and on the recovery from the economic crisis, as well as on the situation in greece and other euro area countries. these are closely linked issues, as the eu's strategy for growth and jobs is linked to these issues. in assessing the current situation, we need to answer the questions: how are the principles of the stability and growth pact being respected in each country? where has the european commission been? it is to be expected that the europe 2020 strategy will be viewed differently by the heads of state or government of the member states. this is due to the fact that there are significant divergences of interests between countries, which in turn arise from differences in levels of development. for obvious reasons, the countries of the last two enlargements, but not only, will fight for a greater emphasis on cohesion policy, infrastructure development or agriculture. but let's not forget about innovation and new technologies. europe's successful development and return to growth over the next decade will depend equally on the achievement of the strategy objectives set out in the commission's proposal, but also on the continuation of more traditional policies. in order to meet the difficult challenges of the global arena, the union must first of all redress its internal imbalances, and this cannot be achieved without respecting the treaty principle of solidarity.
mr. chairman, please! the enhanced role of the european parliament under the lisbon treaty and the european initiative are a very important step towards strengthening european democracy. however, for the initiative to fulfil its role, there must be procedures which do not restrict its democratic nature in the first place. the european parliament currently plays virtually no role in the citizens' initiative process. the previous parliament voted that it is the commission which decides which notified initiatives will be accepted and which rejected. i think the european parliament should play a much greater role here. it should, together with the commission, assess and give an opinion on the initiatives submitted. in this way, decisions on the admissibility of proposed initiatives would also be in the hands of the representatives of the voters, and not only the executive. the european parliament is now the only institution of the european union elected in a free and democratic election, and the citizens' initiative is about people's problems and opinions. if an initiative is rejected by the commission - and therefore by the executive who is supposed to implement it - it can be incomprehensible to the citizens. it is also important that the organiser of the initiative a social organisation, ngo clearly and explicitly states the subject and purpose of the initiative, although it should not necessarily be the one submitting the legislative proposal. i also believe that the procedures for initiatives should be harmonised in the member states, because the diversity of the procedures will make it difficult for us to win broad support for these initiatives.
mr. chairman, please! the public consultation on the european citizens' initiative has now ended and only 323 respondents have participated. this result shows that all the institutions of the european union should now really get involved in promoting this new instrument, because it is clear that very few people are aware of its existence. however, the results of the consultation show the direction in which the commission should go when developing the appropriate implementing rules. first, it is necessary to establish common union-wide rules for collecting and authenticating signatures and to ensure that citizens are subject to the same requirements, for example as regards age. another important issue is the introduction of some form of ex ante admissibility check, assuming that the initiatives and the initiators of the initiatives will be aware that formal recognition of admissibility does not mean that the commission will come forward with a legislative proposal on the matter. i believe that the european citizens' initiative can be an important instrument for future debate, a broad debate on pan-european issues. i look forward to the commission's decision on this.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon gives citizens of the union the right to legislate on their own initiative. this is one of the most important steps in building civic democracy and directly involving citizens in the eu's decision-making process. a european citizens' initiative can help to bridge the gap between the institutions and citizens and support the development of european civil society. it is therefore necessary to adopt swiftly a regulation governing the course, conditions and procedures for the submission of such an initiative. the citizens of the union are looking forward to it. the european citizens' initiative is primarily about making citizens more involved in european law-making. that's why i wanted to bring up the issue of electronic signatures under the citizens' initiative as an additional channel to get people interested in european politics. now that we can vote online, we can do banking online, we can certainly develop a secure system that allows us to identify electronic signatures. transparency of procedures is also important. the organisers of the initiative must be publicly accountable for the transparency of the funding of the signature campaign. even if clear criteria are established for its conduct, this will not prevent the instrument from being abused by eurosceptics, for whom collecting a million signatures with a significant financial commitment, as the last campaign for the european parliament showed, may not be a big problem. the solution could be to require the initiators to maintain a website containing financial information such as sources of income, expenditure, financial statements.
in writing. today's debate is another step towards defining the final shape of the european citizens' initiative. the idea of creating a tool to enable citizens to participate more fully in the democratic life of the union was born in 2005, after the defeat of constitutional referendums in france and the netherlands. these votes reflected a marked lack of communication between the european union and its citizens. even the recently published results of the public consultation launched by the green paper on the european citizens' initiative show little interest from individual citizens. the commission received only 159 responses from individual residents. the citizens' initiative offers an opportunity to change this and to involve our citizens more, by giving them the right to come directly to the commission with proposals for new policy initiatives. to ensure that the initiative does not become a political game, the requirements for citizens must not be too stringent, but the safeguards against abuse must be respected. it is important that the eio is a genuine transnational instrument that is citizen-friendly and easy to use. it should be simple, understandable, and accessible. if the initiative does not meet the formal requirements, the idea should be retained and presented in the form of a petition, so that the work and effort put into preparing it is not wasted. the fulfilment of these conditions will allow europeans, for the first time in the history of an integrated europe, to have a real and direct influence on european policy-making.

the rapporteur. - madam president! - what are you doing? the 2011 budgetary procedure is very specific and exceptional as it concerns the first budgetary year to be established and adopted under the provisions of the treaty of lisbon. we are the pioneers in this field, and we have a special responsibility. the treaty of lisbon gives parliament additional powers in the budgetary field. it is up to us how we use them, and we look forward to a constructive dialogue with both the european commission and the council to make the best and most effective use of these new opportunities provided for by the lisbon treaty. the very important innovation introduced by the lisbon treaty is that we will no longer have two readings of the budget. this means that both parliament and the council will have only single readings. this, of course, poses a particular challenge to discipline. we must be disciplined as a parliament, because we will have - to put it simply - only one chance. we're not gonna have a second reading. we have a lot to settle in the reconciliation meeting. we need to work together and in a disciplined way to ensure that the new budgetary procedure runs smoothly in the autumn. this year is also special because, due to the late election of the european commission, it did not have the opportunity to present its annual political strategy. it is therefore very unique and interesting that the european parliament is the first to express its ideas and that the first opinions on the 2011 budget come from the european parliament in the form of this report, rather than from the european commission, as has been the case every 'normal' year. why is 2011 still so special? the 2011 budget is the fifth budget of the multiannual financial framework. i would remind you that the multiannual financial framework covers the period 2007 to 2013. we have already learned a great deal during the four current budgetary procedures. in polish, you can say we've come to a wall, to a wall. in english, we say we've reached the ceiling. we are in a situation where the multiannual financial framework is running out. we are actually reaching a wall, a point where the margins are very small and any possibilities for parliament are radically reduced. the margins are very small. the figures for section 1b are particularly worrying: around eur 1 million, and for section 3b around eur 9 million. that is why our possibilities are limited, of course, and why the report i have prepared for the committee on budgets so strongly calls for, expects and asks for an ambitious review and revision of the multiannual financial framework. not only because these margins are running out, but also because the revision must take account of the important budgetary implications of the lisbon treaty. the lisbon treaty gives the european union new competences in areas such as space policy. importantly, it also creates a european external action service. there is also a need for budgetary reflection on how we intend to deliver the europe 2020 strategy. all these projects were not foreseen in the multiannual financial framework. we need to start talking now about how to fund these new a general picture in a budgetary context in particular and to issue some guidelines for the administrative budgets of different institutions, including the european parliament and excluding the in writing. the 2011 budget is under discussion, and parliament's amendments to the so-called financial perspective 2007-2013 are being discussed in areas such as 'competitiveness and cohesion for growth and jobs' in addition, we are working on a europe 2020 strategy, which should focus on promoting innovation, supporting entrepreneurship, investing in science, new technologies and regional development. i would like to draw particular attention to the issue of economic, social and territorial cohesion, which is key to ensuring that the eu has sustainable economic growth and full integration of the member states. article 174 of the lisbon treaty mentions mountain policy as a specific type of regional policy alongside island and cross-border regions. in order to promote its harmonious development, the union shall take action to strengthen its economic, social and territorial cohesion. in particular, emphasis should be placed on reducing disparities in levels of development between regions with specific natural and geographical characteristics. mountains and foothills cover almost 40% of the eu's territory and are home to almost 20% of the eu's population. the specific spatial and economic problems of mountain regions require the establishment of transnational legal regulations on the objectives and principles of the specific mountain policies in the member states and, most importantly, the provision of an adequate level of funding for projects and programmes for these regions. i believe that financial support for mountain regions should be included in the new financial perspective and the europe 2020 strategy.
madam president! i would like to point out the relevance of paragraph 9 of mr scott's report, which stresses that the commission should seek to secure an agreement in the wto negotiations on non-trade issues which ensures that imported agricultural products meet the same food safety, animal welfare and environmental protection requirements as those imposed on agricultural products produced in the european union. the problem is that this is the 150th time that the european parliament has spoken out on this issue, to apply the same requirements to importers as to producers in the european union. this has not been addressed and we continue to have a situation where our producers, farmers and manufacturers have to meet high, costly standards, while importers do not meet those standards. this leads to unequal competition. as the report rightly points out, this must change.
mr. chairman, please! thanks to the instruments of the common agricultural policy, the agricultural market in the european union is characterised by a supply of high-quality agri-food products. high standards, good quality food and sufficient supply are what make food safety so important. it is important that the consumer is informed about the quality of the goods. we know that every product that's put on the market has to meet minimum standards. the special quality above the minimum standards must be described on the goods in order to improve their competitiveness by the fact that they have additional qualities for which they have to pay. another important information that should also appear on food products is the place of origin and processing of the raw material. the consumer must know what he is buying and what he is paying for. the lack of this information will weaken the competitiveness of agri-food products produced and processed in europe against imported goods that do not comply with animal welfare, environmental requirements or social standards for working people.

mr. chairman, please! the widespread crisis in the euro area shows the dangers that economic projects, which are not economic in nature but ideological in nature, can pose, especially when integration involves the different economic conditions of individual countries. the question is whether some countries should have joined the euro at that time. the euro project eventually became not so much an economic project as a political one, aimed at speeding up european integration. in many countries, european taxpayers can now pay a heavy price for this haste. it would be good if we could learn from this lesson for the future. the euro is not the answer to the structural problems of individual economies, excessive indebtedness, lack of financial discipline. it is the member states that are responsible for their own finances and these problems should be solved where they arise.
mr. chairman, please! a crisis is a disease that usually leads not only to recovery but also to strengthening and building up immune systems. it can also lead to so-called complications and even some permanent damage to the body. consider how this disease, which we call the crisis, came about. in most cases, the disease is the result of various neglects in our body or comes from outside. the cause of the crisis is the non-market, speculative behavior. the market itself is not able to reject, eliminate or reduce them if there is no proper supervision and monitoring of the processes, and in particular in unusual market situations. until now, financial markets have been monitored and supervised mainly by state, national institutions. globalization has led to the creation of global financial institutions, the global financial market. the commission has not yet developed adequate global, regional, in this case european, institutions to monitor and supervise these markets. the market is not driven by values, but above all by the pursuit of profit at any cost. the crisis did not start in 2008 with a collapse in financial markets, but in 2007 with a crisis in food markets and a disruption in the energy market, which is driven by political instruments. the situation in the european union is the sin of not respecting the established and generally accepted principles of the stability and growth pact. it is a pity that the commission's warnings were too soft. some countries were allowed to do more, because they would be lectured by some commission. some countries have been childish in concealing their sins. that's not what community is about, and that's not what integration is about. it is important to admit the mistakes that have been made, to inform our citizens, to apologize to them, to ask for understanding and cooperation in overcoming the crisis. we must take action to ensure that the costs of the crisis are not passed on to the weakest and poorest. our duty of eu solidarity is also to support the countries most affected by the crisis. healing will not come from outside if the organism, the state, does not take up the fight.

in writing. - in my speech i spoke about the situation in the euro area and public finances in 2009. my verdict on the vote has a broader context. as forecast by economists, 2009 proved to be the most difficult year for the member states affected by the crisis. the union's gdp fell by 4%, industrial production by 20%, the number of unemployed rose to 23 million, and so on. the costs of combating the crisis have led to a drastic deterioration in the state of public finances. however, some countries already had high public debt levels before the recession, which were contrary to the stability and growth pact. the financial crisis has proved to be the greatest challenge the euro area has ever faced. it has laid bare the weaknesses of the single currency system. the most serious of these is undoubtedly the wide variation in the stability of public finances and the level of debt in the euro area. the stability and growth pact, which was supposed to guarantee the fulfilment of the convergence criteria, has suddenly been disregarded by national and eu authorities alike. the lack of discipline and an adequate system of penalties eventually led to the single currency crisis. many politicians who are unwilling to see european economic integration have already announced the break-up of the eurozone, spreading visions of disaster for the entire integration process. however, i believe that these views are unfounded and speculative. the euro area is facing a major reform opportunity that will improve control mechanisms and ensure greater coordination. it's just a matter of being reasonable about the process.

in writing. − i would like to express my satisfaction that the rapporteur has included in the draft recommendation of the european parliament to the council on the eu priorities for the 65th session of the united nations general assembly issues relating to such an important topic as un-eu cooperation in crisis management. more recently, the earthquakes in haiti and chile have shown how vulnerable people are to the suffering and damage caused by natural disasters. however, in both countries, eu and un cooperation has been successful in rescuing and assisting those affected. i believe that we should now focus on optimising this cooperation in order to make the best use of the resources available and to save as many people as possible as quickly as possible, and to enable them to survive later. in addition, assistance to maintain order and rebuild the country after the disaster is also a key issue. although all eu member states are also members of the un and the european community has permanent observer status at the un, there are difficulties in developing a harmonised position for all eu countries. i believe that a common constructive approach to effective cooperation in disaster relief is a priority.
in writing. - discrimination against roma has been one of the main taboos in europe for years. in recent years, it has been breaking down. measures to combat discrimination against roma are still insufficient. often this problem is met with disregard. a good example of this is the european commission's lack of response to the european parliament's request of 28 january 2008 to develop a european roma strategy in cooperation with the member states. the need of the moment is to reiterate that conclusion. in times of economic crisis, aggression against the roma is on the rise. it affects many of the 10-12 million roma in the european union. recognising that roma issues should be given priority status by the newly appointed commissioners, i decided to support the draft resolution on the second european roma summit prepared by the s&d and ppe members.
in writing. - building the eu budget in a time of financial crisis, with a very tight budgetary margin and new challenges associated with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, is not easy. i was all the more pleased to vote in favour of the report by sidonia jędrzewska on the 2011 budget and the ep's draft resolution, both of which set out ambitious budgetary priorities for the coming year. in addition to traditional priorities such as cohesion policy and the promotion of innovative and green technologies, the 2011 budget should focus on ensuring the full operability of new initiatives in the eu: the european external action service, the eu 2020 economic strategy and the eastern partnership actions. all three are threatened with failure if the measures planned for them prove too "symbolic". the comprehensive approach to the youth problem is also noteworthy. in the face of demographic problems, the eu cannot afford a low rate of educated youth, as this would lead to an even greater increase in unemployment in this age group, which the union simply cannot afford. the european budget must therefore allocate funds to support language learning, intercultural dialogue, increase the mobility of young people and the integration of graduates into the labour market.

in writing. − the report of the development committee on the impact of the global financial and economic crisis on developing countries and on development cooperation rightly notes that in the last two years there has been not one but a series of interrelated crises. the situation should not lead to a reduction but to an increase in development aid to developing countries. the common objective should be to allocate 0,56% of gross national income to development aid by 2010 and 0,7% by 2015. beyond immediate relief, what is needed is action to change the architecture of the world economic order. hence my support for the immediate implementation of the commitment made at the g20 summit in pittsburgh to give at least 5% of the shares in the imf to emerging and developing countries and at least 3% of the voting rights in the world bank to developing and transition countries. these actions should be linked to the action taken to eliminate tax havens. the tobin tax is also an important systemic solution that is worth considering. given that the commission's report contains all the above-mentioned points, i have decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. − the ecb's annual report for 2008 reflects well the causes and conditions of the crisis. the year 2008, which saw the onset of the most severe phase of the economic crisis in decades, determined the direction of the world and european economies for a long time to come. the last two years have undoubtedly been the most difficult in the history of the european central bank. the bank was faced with a crisis that had a severe impact on the european economy. the increasing budget deficits in the member states, combined with the growing debt burden, are the main consequences of the macroeconomic crisis. under the treaty, the ecb has primary responsibility for price stability, or low inflation. has the bank fulfilled its task? it's hard to say for sure. while the current inflation rate is within the ecb's ceiling, it should be noted that it reached the highest level in the euro area's history in the first months of the crisis, before falling sharply thereafter. but i think that this instability can be explained by the surprise of the crisis. since october 2008, the ecb's monetary policy can be described as active and flexible. the ecb adopted a different strategy for the crisis than other leading central banks around the world. we are still awaiting the results of these activities. europe is emerging from the crisis, but the situation is still uncertain. is the ecb prepared for the possibility of another crisis, as some economists see it?

in writing. in the face of the demographic processes taking place in europe among the local population and the economic crisis, a well-designed strategic action plan has my full support. the europe 2020 strategy should enable us to effectively combat the effects of these negative developments so that our continent is ready to face the challenges of the next decade in a globally competitive environment. i hope that a good information campaign will be carried out among the citizens of the member states so that they can use the powers granted to them by the lisbon treaty and influence the planning and then the implementation of the strategy through actions at regional, county, municipal, municipal and smaller local community level. i agree that the strategic priorities themselves - sustainable growth, a knowledge-based and innovative economy, investment in citizens' education and building a society free of economic divisions and poverty - are well articulated. this should be followed by the rapid development of the implementation mechanisms and the establishment of the implementation timetable. i look forward to a good, comprehensive cooperation in this area. i stress that the europe 2020 strategy must take account of the huge differences in the level of development and potential of the different regions. if we forget to adapt the timetable and the means of achieving our strategic objectives to the specific characteristics of the different parts of the eu, i fear that our work may not produce the results we expect.
in writing. the 2020 strategy adopted by the european council is unacceptable to me as a socialist. the strategic objective (combating poverty) and the means to achieve it are not clearly defined. poverty affects 80 million (20%) of europeans. 17% have incomes so low that they can't meet their basic needs. it's not just an economic problem, it's a human rights violation. poverty leads to health loss, to lack of access to education, to homelessness, to discrimination, to social exclusion. according to a 2008 report by the european commission, one in five poles (19%) live below the poverty line and 26% of children live in poverty (the highest rate in the union). we need a long-term strategy to fight poverty as an integral part of eu policy. the strategy should be supported by reform of the common agricultural policy, as proposed by my group. it is necessary to ensure food security in all its aspects (physical and economic availability of food meeting high health and quality requirements) for all union citizens. the 2020 strategy will only be a valuable document for eu citizens if it takes social objectives into account. i therefore ask the commission and the council to: 1. make the fight against poverty the main strategic objective of action; 2. set and precisely quantify specific objectives for the systematic reduction of poverty; 3. develop and adopt (at the june summit) specific indicators; 4. set deadlines for the achievement of the individual sub-objectives.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the last european summit was an attempt to develop a new strategy for the euro area and to get out of the economic crisis. european leaders agreed that economic policy coordination in europe should be strengthened by defining future common guidelines and developing an early warning system for member states in the face of economic problems. the aftermath of the global financial crisis is a good opportunity for europe to strengthen its internal integration and cooperation. now is the time to take advantage of the undeniable benefits of european integration and take the european project to the next level. the summit was optimistic and promising, but we must be careful that this attempt to devise a new economic strategy for europe does not end up as spectacularly as the lisbon strategy, which was supposed to transform the european union into the most dynamic knowledge-based economy. thank you. thank you.
in writing. there is no doubt that the situation of the greek economy is causing a lot of excitement. its catastrophic state is both a result of the global crisis and the negligence of the government in athens. this is due to the lack of major reforms and the too loose interpretation of macroeconomic data. greece is on the verge of bankruptcy today. the country will suffer the effects of today's economic collapse for many years to come. i therefore looked with great interest at the proposed forms of support which the council intends to provide to greece. i am glad that this country can count on aid, but it should be combined with immediate and radical reforms of public finances. our response to the crisis in greece must be a clear signal to other member states facing similar problems that strong internal reforms are the way out.

in writing. the delegation procedure, although it remains in the shadows, is a very important qualitative change introduced by the lisbon treaty. it should be seen as complementary to the treaty, without which parliament's position vis-à-vis the other institutions in the decision-making process will not be fully strengthened. only through this procedure will we gain full legislative powers and insight into the process of implementing the legislation in question. we are well aware of the frustration of the arduous process of negotiating with the council in the codecision procedure and of the uncompromising implementation of a decision. until now, 'comitology' has been an expression of member states' lack of confidence in the commission, but now parliament's insight into the implementation of a given legal act gives this process greater legitimacy. parliament and, indirectly, eu citizens will be closer to implementing eu law, and this is how we should view the delegation procedure. but for it to make sense, parliament must have full access to information, and i agree entirely with the participants in the debate.
in writing. the introduction of the delegation of legislative power is intended to ensure that legislation, especially of a technical nature, is supplemented and updated more efficiently without the need to initiate a full legislative procedure. delegation of power should therefore be seen as a tool for better eu lawmaking. at the same time, it is necessary to ensure appropriate control of the commission's use of the powers conferred on it. parliament and the council must, inter alia, have sufficient time to exercise their right to object to the proposed regulation. however, they must first of all have appropriate access to the documents, analyses and opinions produced during the preparatory work for the draft delegated acts. only in this way can the commission's power to adopt delegated acts genuinely contribute to streamlining the legislative process in the union, while maintaining the necessary control and transparency of the commission's activities. at the same time, it is necessary to develop appropriate cooperation mechanisms between parliament and the commission so that parliament is kept up to date on the preparatory work in progress and has the opportunity to gain a good understanding of the substance of the issues under consideration. the resolution on delegation of legislative powers, which is the result of a compromise between all political groups, properly addresses these issues and deserves the support of parliament.
member of the commission. − madam president, i thank mrs ţicău for her very positive evaluation of the approach to the blacklist. the commission is convinced that the existing measures already provide for a very high level of information and rights to the public for flights within and outside the european union. the list of airlines banned within the european union is made widely available to the public on the internet and by targeted information actions. the commission liaises closely with european and international travel agent associations each time the list is updated. this allows them to be in the best possible position to aid the passengers. national civil aviation authorities and airports in the territory of member states are obliged to bring the eu list to the attention of passengers, both via their websites and, where relevant, on their premises as well. the list provides useful information to people wishing to travel outside the european union in order for them to avoid travelling with these airlines. the list has no extra-territorial effect – it does not apply outside the european union. hence, the regulation establishes passengers’ rights to know the identity of every airline they fly with throughout their trip. the contracting carrier – or travel agent or tour operator – is required to inform passengers when making a reservation of the identity of the air carrier or carriers effectively operating the flight. the passenger must also be kept informed of any change of operating carrier, either at check-in or, at the latest, when boarding. the regulation also gives passengers the right to reimbursement or re-routing if a carrier with which a booking has been made is subsequently added to the list, resulting in cancellation of the flight concerned. different sources of information are used to monitor and assess the compliance of operators with international safety standards, namely the safety audits carried out by the international civil aviation organisation, the information provided by competent authorities of third countries, the information provided by the european aviation safety agency in the framework of its inspections and investigations within the european union or technical missions outside the european union, the results of the ramp checks carried out on aircraft or air carriers at eu airports in the framework of the safety assessment of foreign aircraft programme, according to the requirements of the relevant eu rules, and, finally, substantiated accident-related information stemming from accident or serious incident investigation reports. i should also mention that the european commission does not at this stage have a comprehensive list of the countries which have similar legislation but several states – the republic of korea, bahrain and the kingdom of saudi arabia – apply the same restrictions as those defined in the european list. i can confirm that the commission is ready to work with parliament to really improve this blacklist legislation, but it provides for much-needed safety in the air.
on behalf of the ecr group. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: i hope, but there is no guarantee that the effects of the icelandic volcano will not be passed on to european passengers in terms of ticket prices, because indeed you are right, these disruptions in air traffic will be compensated for by probably higher ticket prices. this is worth saying in the interest of the european consumer. the european parliament is once again taking a vote on this matter. it's a reflection of how much we care. i spoke about this a few months ago, and many of you also spoke about it then, i remember the last parliament, and we also spoke about it very loudly then. and then, a personal reflection: one of the journalists of the most influential polish newspaper asked me: what do you do in the european parliament, after all, it is such an insignificant matter. it was only with time that the media began to become aware of the fact that this was a very important issue, a security issue and an absolutely fundamental issue from the point of view of the interests of european citizens, taxpayers, voters and consumers. it is unnatural that we know what the blacklist is like inside the european union and we don't know what it is like outside the european union. this is a completely schizophrenic situation. the last very important point: it cannot be that european passengers pay extra for safety, but this is a matter for the states and governments.

president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report. i have the honour and pleasure to present to you today the first work programme of this commission, which is also the first work programme since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. i have the honour and pleasure of doing so with virtually my entire team, the european commission, as a sign of respect for your parliament. this programme is being presented at a crucial moment for europe, because now is the time to act. this programme is a direct result of our political dialogue. after intensive consultations based on the political guidelines i have put forward for the next five years, this parliament gave me responsibility for a second term in september. after extensive hearings, which helped to forge a common vision of the actions to be taken, the college as a whole was entrusted to you in february. in other words, this work programme shows a strong convergence with the political priorities expressed by your institution. as such, it provides a solid platform for achieving ambitious results. our first priority must be to get out of the crisis and to lay the foundations for sustainable growth and job creation. first, the urgent questions: we have recently discussed the outcome of the european council. in the meantime, the announced financial support mechanism for greece was finally put into place on 11 april. the commission will play an important role in the implementation of this mechanism when greece requests its activation. this is the logical consequence of the fact that the commission has been heavily involved, from the outset, in finding a solution to the financial problems facing greece and in maintaining stability within the euro area. we have always done so in accordance with the principles of solidarity but also responsibility. but we need to do more than ask why these problems arose and how to prevent them from happening again. that is why we will review the stability and growth pact to deepen economic surveillance and extend it beyond the deficit issue alone. we need a permanent mechanism for resolving crises. in short, we must show that the european union - and the euro area in particular - is up to the challenges of the moment and we must exploit all the opportunities offered by the lisbon treaty. that is why one of the first major initiatives of the commission next month will be to present a communication on the enhanced coordination of economic policies. we all know that the collective interest of europe is at stake here. the union must strengthen the system and take account of the full range of economic risks and imbalances. we need to improve the internal mechanisms. by having stronger structures and a better coordinated approach, europe can facilitate the return of public finances to a sustainable trajectory and create a framework for a broader and more sustainable recovery. ladies and gentlemen, over the last eighteen months we have made enormous progress towards a more ethical, sound and responsible financial system. we must persevere on this path, filling the remaining regulatory gaps and ensuring that our supervisory structures keep pace with a constantly changing industry. i am convinced that our proposal on alternative and private equity funds will soon reach a decisive stage. the commission believes that the legislator will support our common objective of ensuring that the new european architecture for financial sector supervision is fully operational by the beginning of next year. in 2010, the commission intends to present several proposals in key areas such as derivatives markets, deposit guarantee schemes and market abuse. the protection of ordinary consumers of financial services will receive particular attention. we will also work on other major aspects of cds and short selling and will soon propose guidelines on the establishment of bank insolvency resolution funds. mr president, distinguished members of parliament, this commission hit the ground running. by presenting the europe 2020 strategy right after taking office, we have set the scene to help bring europe back on track on track for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. we now need to work together european parliament, member states, commission to build and sustain the momentum. achieving the vision of a sustainable social market economy by 2020 will require a strong effort from all levels of decision-making and all levels of society. at european level, our action must have genuine european added-value. this is the goal of the europe 2020 flagship initiatives the digital agenda for europe, a full-fledged industrial policy, a european plan for research and innovation, a resource-efficient europe, new skills for new jobs, youth on the move, fighting social exclusion. this is where europe can make the difference. thus we will help drive the transition to a resource efficient and climate-change resilient economy. fighting climate change will remain a top priority on our agenda, both internally and globally. the energy and transport sectors will get particular attention this year both critical to turn the challenge of a sustainable europe into our competitive advantage. the single market, as a home market of 500 million consumers underpinning jobs, competitiveness, affordable prices and consumer choice, will continue to be the backbone of the european economy. tapping its full potential is particularly important for small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the most important driver for job creation in the european union. bringing the single market into the 21st century is a priority for the commission, which will make new proposals by 2012. this is also the subject of a report which i have asked mario monti to prepare and which we will be presenting very soon. i want to underline the importance of social inclusion in our vision for europe 2020. the real strength of a society rests on the opportunities it creates for its weakest citizens. we must seize every opportunity to encourage employment and social cohesion. that means being ready to exploit the emerging sectors which will generate new jobs. it means providing people with the right skills to create and sustain high employment levels and facilitate economic transition. it means working to overcome the impact of the crisis on young people by easing transitions from education and training to work. to this end, a broad-ranging european platform against poverty will be built on the current european year for combating poverty and social exclusion. this agenda is of course a contribution to the fulfilment of our principles of economic, social and territorial cohesion. the concerns and well-being of european citizens will remain at the heart of commission action. the implementation of a comprehensive action plan of the stockholm programme that the commission will be adopting later today is focused precisely on ensuring that the benefits of european integration in the area of freedom, security and justice become more tangible to the citizens. this action plan represents on its own a comprehensive work programme for the commission in the area of freedom, security and justice. it puts citizens at the core of our policies by facilitating the exercise of their specific rights. it will also aim at developing an open and secure europe with a particular focus on tackling cross-border crime and on a common immigration and asylum policy. in the field of freedom, security and justice, the european union has in the last 10 years gone from the application of the free movement of persons to a common policy. the achievements so far have been impressive but we need, more than ever in this period of exit from the crisis, to promote and defend european values and indeed, above all, to tap all the potential that is now created by the lisbon treaty. the action plan contains a comprehensive list of measures to implement our already defined priorities in this field, both at european and global level. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty also gives us the tools to demonstrate greater ambition. the increased role of this parliament, more efficient decision-making in the council, the prospect of more coherence and consistency of member states in european council decisions, and judicial review by the court of justice will strengthen the european union's determination to respond to the expectations and concerns of our citizens. when we look to 2020, we must also address a number of long-term trends with a direct impact on the daily lives of citizens. action now will pay dividends in the future. for example, the commission will launch a public debate on the future of pensions and analyse options for ensuring the sustainability and adequacy of pension systems. of course, in any area like this many of the levers are national but that must not hold us back from ensuring that the european union makes a maximum contribution. in the external field, the new role of the high representative/vice-president and the start of the european external action service will offer us the tools to build a stronger and more coherent eu external policy. we will set out strategic trade policy priorities, take forward trade negotiations and work with partners on issues ranging from market access to regulatory framework and global imbalances. we will project our europe 2020 objectives on the global market place, for example through the g20. the commission will also be tackling the challenges of energy geopolitics, in order to ensure safe, secure, sustainable and affordable energy. another key priority for the commission is to pursue the international development agenda and propose an eu action plan in the run-up to the 2015 millennium development goals summit. this initiative will form the basis for the june european council to prepare a common eu position in view of the high level united nations review meeting in september on the millennium development goals (mdgs), which aims at the adoption of a global action plan for reaching the mdgs by 2015. we want a europe that is open and shows in concrete actions its solidarity with the most vulnerable in the world. finally, as agreed with this parliament, we will publish the budget review during the third semester of this year. in this we will set out what we see as the key principles and parameters for using the european union's financial resources to best effect, taking full account of the europe 2020 strategy. in parallel, we will be making more detailed assessments of key areas, including agriculture and cohesion. i can assure you that parliament will be fully associated at all stages of the budget review. before finishing, i would like to briefly explain a number of innovations in the work programme. this programme, and future programmes, need to offer the right framework for the institutions to build a solid consensus on where europe should focus its attention. we therefore need to be more political, and we also need to reflect the multiannual challenge of initiatives of the scale we intend. i think the way we prepare the work programmes in the future should be a concrete demonstration of the special partnership which i and the commission want to establish with the european parliament in this mandate. this programme identifies 34 strategic initiatives that we are committed to putting on the table before the end of december. i'm sure you agree that this is an ambitious agenda for the next eight months. at the same time, the programme includes many other initiatives for 2010 and beyond. this indicative list includes initiatives on which the commission intends to work over the coming years. not all of these initiatives will necessarily lead to the submission of concrete proposals. in line with the principles of smart regulation, we need to assess thoroughly which items should go forward, and in which form. the work programme will be reviewed every year to identify new strategic initiatives and adapt the multi-annual strand as required. this 'rolling' approach will enhance transparency and predictability for all stakeholders, while preserving the necessary flexibility to react to unforeseen developments. one thing we've learned in recent years is that we should always predict the unpredictable. recent years have shown that strategic blueprints cannot be cast in stone they have to adapt to reality on the ground. honourable members, the commission work programme for 2010 that we are proud to present today is an ambitious, but also necessary and realistic, framework for european policy-making in the coming year. it is realistic if all institutions are ready to join forces and cooperate with a view to delivering timely results to europe's citizens; it is necessary because business as usual is not an option if we want 2010 to mark a turning point; and it is ambitious because, more than ever, a strong europe is required to deliver to citizens the solutions they are looking for. they expect it from us, and we have a duty to work for their prosperity and well-being.

staying power. this is really important because if we move too quickly to reconstruction, away from support for people in need, we risk a very serious tragedy. we had to deal with this in the issue of food delivery where the government of haiti suggested that we shift away from food provision to only cash-for-work and food-for-work, which is highly desirable but cannot be done everywhere at the same time. this is something we are watching very closely. broadly, on the issue of food security, our new policy in the european union is very progressive because it emphasises all other things equally, encouraging local purchase of food for humanitarian aid whenever it is possible to get it locally. we have made this topic subject to a discussion in a morning session in new york where we invited ngos, haitian as well as international ngos, and i was very proud that it was the european ngos that put these issues of agricultural security for haiti and high agricultural return in productivity for the discussion in haiti. i want to address the issue of shelter. it is not at all a trivial issue because people actually do not want to move from where they are now. they do not want to move for a variety of reasons. one, even if their houses are safe they are afraid to go back because of the trauma they experienced. two, because they moved as whole neighbourhoods and they are scared of losing the social fabric that keeps them together, so it is not just bad policy or lack of desire, it is also the social phenomenon that follows a disaster of this nature that makes it not so easy to get people to move from flood-prone areas to safer ground. but we are addressing this as a priority. let me finish with the question of long-term sustainability. it is governance sustainability, it is also ecological sustainability. i had the dubious privilege to fly over haiti and chile, within a couple of weeks of each other. in haiti, an ecologically destroyed island, of course it had implications for the scale of this destruction. in chile, the government has implemented for decades a reafforestation programme stabilising the soil and, as a result, creating a better environment, which is obviously very helpful for people. we are thinking in the long term when we think of chile. this is not in my area but i have to pick it up as a former world bank employee. i certainly agree with you that what the world bank is proposing about this coordination in the multi-donor trust fund but also as an institutional project management approach is something that we need to take to heart and follow.
member of the commission. − mr president, as usual, if i had just one wish in my political life, it would be to have more time in parliament to answer the questions i am asked. i will not be able to in writing. ladies and gentlemen, we are gathered here today to discuss european coordination of aid to haiti, while international commentators are criticizing our uncoordinated actions. it's been three months since the tragic earthquake and it still seems we can't work out a common position on support for haiti. in january we heard a lot of speeches about the union's role on the international stage, but it is a shame to see how weak and indecisive the union has been so far. the european union's allocation of eur 1.2 billion in aid to haiti is commendable. global donors have pledged $5.3 billion over two years to help haiti rebuild. in the longer term, the aid is expected to increase to usd 9.9 billion. that's a very optimistic figure! but the haitian cataclysm made me reflect and think about this long-dead nation. the earthquake was a natural disaster, but the current level of poverty is the result of economic, political and social collapse. the decline and violence in haiti in recent years is the result of centuries of brutal relations with the outside world: some states and international corporations. haiti has failed the international community, let's do more to rehabilitate now.

president of the commission. − you are basically right in your analysis regarding the situation in the labour market. in fact, the situation is continuing to deteriorate, even if it is at a more moderate pace than in the past. we are also starting to see more consistent signs of stabilisation in some member states. but it has been nine months since the economy started to recover from deep recession and it may take some time this year before the fragile pick-up in economic activity has an impact on reversing the trend in the labour market. that is why our priority is now employment. for young people, unemployment is particularly worrying, as you said. we have more than 20% of young people unemployed in europe. that is why we have launched three initiatives for this year. two of them i have already mentioned. there is also the youth employment initiative. among the specific initiatives that we are going to develop is precisely the step-up of vocational training through more apprenticeship schemes, financed by the european social fund and also fostering high-quality learning experience in the workplace after graduation, the so-called traineeships, including the possibility of traineeships in other member states.
president of the commission. − i am aware of that report of the european climate foundation and, indeed, under the 2020 strategy we have proposed a resource-efficient europe flagship initiative whose aim is precisely to decouple growth from resources, giving europe a competitive advantage compared to other international partners. this objective was also fully translated in the commission’s working programme for 2010 and beyond. it is the commission’s intention to develop a path for europe’s transition to a low-carbon, resource-efficient and climate-change resilient economy by 2050, particularly through the decarbonisation of the energy and transport sectors, thus providing a long-term framework for policy and investment. i underline the word investment. we believe that the climate agenda can also be, as the renewable energy sector is showing, a way of creating more jobs in europe, what we usually call ‘green jobs’.
president of the commission. − the european digital library, addressing the challenge of putting online the collections of our national libraries, museums and their archives, this is a major task of our times digitising, making available, preserving the wealth of our culture. yet we have to do it without jeopardising the rights of authors and publishers, including out-of-print works and for so-called ‘orphan’ works. we also have to assess whether our financial efforts and the public-private partnerships that are being experienced here and there are up to this very important societal challenge. in this perspective, i have asked vice-president kroes and commissioner vassiliou to set up a comité des sages. i am happy to announce today to you that mr maurice lavie, mrs elizabeth nigerman and mr jacques decare will be entrusted with this task. as a comité des sages, they will promote this idea of keeping our very important heritage through digitisation, in full respect of course of the property rights. i look forward to receiving their recommendations on these important issues by the end of this year.
mr. chairman of the commission! i'd like to know how you feel the recent downturn in the airline industry will affect your employment. today, the front page of the highly influential financial times reports that this outage, which has grounded nearly 7 million passengers and caused the cancellation of 80,000 flights, is costing the airline industry $200 million a day. how do you think that translates into employment in this sector, because i understand that was the main reason for your absence and mr. van rompuy's absence from the funeral of the polish president in krakow.
president of the commission. − we are not forcing anyone to take any measures. regarding greece, decisions were taken by the greek authorities, but you will certainly understand that this situation of macroeconomic imbalances in the greek economy is very negative for growth and also for employment. it is clear that without a restoration of confidence in greece’s public finances, there will be no investment or growth in greece. without growth we cannot generate employment. that is why we should not set macroeconomic stability and rigour in contradiction or opposition to growth. the problem is to see how we can manage a transition, how we can keep stimulus in the economies that have the margin to do it, and at the same time respect the necessary balances of macroeconomic stability. that is why it is in the interests of the greek economy and of greek workers for greece’s public finances to have credibility as soon as possible.
president of the commission. − this volcano problem is certainly beyond the control of the european institutions or the national governments. it happened and now we have to react to its consequences. regarding the aviation industry, we have already said that we are looking at what we can do, also based on the precedent that was already there after 11 september. regarding the economic situation, i think it is too soon to make an overall assessment of the damage caused, and it is probably better to avoid very dramatic – or let us say, panic – scenarios. what we believe is important now is to address the damage and to try to see what we can do at european level, bearing in mind one important thing – at european level we are responsible for one per cent of the public budget. the other 99% is in the hands of the member states. so i think it is unfair to look to the european union to try to solve all the problems, where we do not have the means to do so.
mr. chairman, please! in your 2020 strategy, you set very ambitious targets to increase employment from 63% to 76%, to reduce youth unemployment to 10% and to focus on education, which is the key to achieving a future where 40% of europeans have a higher education. so my question is: will the european social fund and the research and development funds be retained in the future budget of the european union, which is the key to modernity, innovation and employment? do you not think that the development of micro-enterprises should also be encouraged, since this is the best way of self-employment, and today the rates of self-employment are still too low and therefore these questions seem appropriate in this context?
president of the commission. − yes, you know we have proposed education as one of the targets in the eu2020, including fighting against early school leaving and having more tertiary education. we believe it is impossible to discuss european competitiveness without addressing the issue of education. that is why we are trying to convince all member states to accept that target and, certainly, afterwards there has to be a mobilisation of resources, some from member states and some from the european union. we have to discuss afterwards the financial perspective. we are not yet there but, certainly, i think some actions should also be taken at european level, complementing the efforts made by the national governments. indeed, in the social fund, we already have some actions for young people for apprenticeships and for traineeships. this is our intention. we cannot anticipate what funds will be available for the social fund but, certainly, we believe that we should have adequate ambition at the european instruments’ level.
president of the commission. − the employment guidelines are very much dependent on the overall economic growth, but we intend to reinforce the employment aspect in our eu 2020 strategy. in fact we have four guidelines: increasing labour market participation and reducing structural unemployment, developing a skilled workforce, promoting job quality and lifelong learning, improving the performance of the education systems and increasing the participation in socioeducation, as well as combating poverty and social exclusion. these are general guidelines that have now to be pursued by the european institutions with all the instruments they have at their disposal, and by national governments. it is true that there is no silver bullet, there is no magical solution or panacea for unemployment in europe. it has to come also from the overall measures taken for growth in terms of respect for financial stability, in terms of confidence in our markets, in terms of tapping the potential of the internal market. that is the only way to do it. when it comes to the automobile industry, of course we know that there was over-capacity not only in europe but in the world, and we are following this very closely with the industry itself, including with the trade unions in the sector.
president of the commission. − i want to win this competitiveness battle globally. one thing is sure: we need more people, working more and longer – and i would add, better, in a more competitive way. there is no contradiction between having longer working lives and having some immigration to europe. in fact, it is quite extraordinary, but today there are almost one million job vacancies in germany and almost half a million in the uk. this shows that there is a problem of mismatch between the supply and demand for labour. there is a lot to do in this area. i believe that pension reforms are also a way of contributing to that. i want to underline that, during this crisis, member states did not resort to the traditional policy of having people leave the workforce earlier. they have not done so. in fact it has been possible to keep people in work for longer. this is important because, for europe to remain competitive, we need to raise the employment rate in europe.
mr. chairman, please! in your speech today you mentioned that one of the commission's priorities in employment policy is to help graduates, young people, to enter the labour market effectively. we know that the unemployment rate in this social group is very high today. in spain it is now almost 40%, in poland 20% and unfortunately it is constantly increasing. the problem seems to be the lack of adaptation of education courses to the needs of the labour market and the poor availability of initial vocational training. in your opinion, can we speak of a low effectiveness of the leonardo da vinci vocational education and training programme? how do you rate this program? is the european commission preparing new measures, if so, what are they to prevent the increase in youth unemployment? what can you, mr president barroso, offer and propose to young people in europe today?
president of the commission. − youth unemployment is the most dramatic problem now in unemployment in europe because it is more than 20%. that is why we have announced three concrete initiatives: ‘youth on the move’, ‘youth employment’ and ‘new skills for new jobs’. ‘youth on the move’ to improve efficiency and equity of european education and training systems; ‘youth employment’ to look at ways to overcome the impact of the crisis on young people and ‘new skills for new jobs’ to better match skills and labour supply with demand. i have just highlighted the situation in two of the largest member states in europe because, by 2020, 16 million more jobs will require high qualifications and, for example, the european social fund will spend eur 13.5 million, between 2007 and 2013, in promoting adaptability measures for workers and enterprises. so there are some measures that we can take at european level, community level, to complement the action of our member states regarding the problem of youth unemployment.
president of the commission. − i have to remind you that it was the commission that launched the climate change and energy package and that we have highlighted the great potential for the creation of jobs in some sectors of the so-called greening of the economy and that, certainly, the priority for the future is such, one of the most important targets of the eu 2020. we have put at the centre of the eu 2020 our climate and energy targets, from 20% reduction of greenhouse gases, to 20% renewables and to 20% gains in energy efficiency. for instance, to have this target of 20% renewables, we are going to create jobs throughout the renewables sector. so it is certainly the central piece of our economic strategy for the future and, in fact, we have put that as one of the core objectives. growth, not only smart growth and equitable growth, but also sustainable growth.

the european personnel selection office, known as epso, is the interinstitutional body responsible for recruiting staff to the institutions of the european union. i am very pleased that the discharge reports deal with this subject. efforts are needed to explore and address geographical disparities among candidates and laureates for the civil service of the european union institutions. the continued under-representation of citizens of the new member states, including poland, but not only among the civil service of the european union is particularly unacceptable. this is particularly striking in my view among middle and senior management. the very long recruitment process and the management of the so-called laureate lists also raise doubts. often, the winners of the competitions - those who have been successful in the competition - take up other jobs outside the eu institutions because they simply cannot wait that long, and the whole recruitment process is wasted. i am pleased that epso has drawn up a corrective programme and has taken account of the court of auditors' observations and that epso has already taken account of some of the european parliament's observations. i will certainly be following the effects of this corrective programme closely, always remembering that epso's aim should be first and foremost to reach the best candidates as possible with the institution's offer, to select the best candidates as possible, to create the best lists of laureates proportionally representing all member states.

in writing. - as a member of the committee on culture and education, i support the report 'europeana' next steps'. europeana, by linking the digital resources of europe's national libraries, provides a digital access point to the cultural and scientific heritage of humanity. the project was supported by the association of polish librarians. the successful implementation of this project requires stable funding to guarantee the participation of national libraries and the universal availability of europeana resources. only 5% of europe's cultural heritage is now available in digital form almost half (47%) come from france, 6% from germany and 5% each from the netherlands and the united kingdom. the project assumes that 10 million digital materials will be available from june 2010 and 15 million in 2011. to enable this, the funding for the digitisation of cultural products should be increased, ensuring close cooperation between copyright holders, cultural institutions, the public and private sectors. to ensure that europeana is used by as many people as possible, the materials must be available in all the official languages of the european union. an information campaign is needed to raise awareness of europeana. the portal must also take into account the needs of people with disabilities to enable them to have full access to common european knowledge. in this context, the european commission and individual publishers should provide special digital versions of works, such as audio, to people with disabilities.
in writing. - i believe that the creation of the europeana multimedia online library is a very important step in the process of digitising european and world cultural heritage. that is why i supported the report by helga trupel. the project provides access to over four and a half million books, videos, maps and magazines, photographs and music, and is an archive that preserves for future generations content previously written on paper, canvas or parchment, which is extremely valuable for both ordinary citizens and scientists, making it easier for them to access rare and hard-to-reach works. the lack of uniformity in copyright law in the member states is a major obstacle to the further development of europeana. we should strive to standardise the law so that as many works as possible are available to citizens, while ensuring that creators are fairly remunerated. the success of this project will depend to a large extent on the continued financial commitment of the member states.

madam president, i strongly disagree with the previous speaker. this house had to answer a question on whether or not we should convene a convention to decide that issue, and we have taken a decision not to do so, but we have done so out of respect for this instrument – for this new instrument, which actually increases the legitimacy of all the decisions which we make. obviously that does not set a precedent for the future, because all the really important issues concerning the changes to the treaty, such as for example the electoral procedure, would require the convening of a convention. let me thank íñigo and the coordinators for taking the decision. it was not easy. we had a problem with designating an additional 18 members of this house because certain member states did not actually plan for a procedure, but we decided that representativeness is the most important issue, that this is the principle which we should be guided by and that this house should have a balanced representation as quickly as possible. that is why we took a pragmatic solution, prompting member states to complete their election procedures as quickly as possible, provided, obviously, that all the parliamentarians who are going to join us are going to be directly elected.
the treaty of lisbon has changed the composition of the european parliament. although it has been in force for six months, no intergovernmental conference has yet been convened to implement these changes. member states must ratify the special protocol with an additional number of mandates. it's a big operation, but it doesn't change the fact that the treaty must be implemented in full, without delay. i agree with the rapporteur's position on this matter. it should be borne in mind that it is in the interests of the member states whose national delegations are enlarged by the treaty that their new members should be able to represent their constituents as soon as possible. this is in line with the fundamental democratic principles on which the union is founded. it is important that all additional meps enter parliament at the same time to avoid any allegations of the improper functioning of our institution.
