madam president! i would like to begin by saying how pleased i am that the european parliament has dealt with this matter in its own-initiative report. i would like to offer my warmest congratulations to mr karas. in the last decade, we have seen the development of all kinds of financial innovations, new instruments, unprecedented. these instruments often determine the face of the market today. it seems that the essential precondition for effective supervision in this situation is to have a really honest knowledge of what is happening in these markets. the financial instruments that have become popular have reached a level of complexity that makes it very difficult for supervisors to properly assess the risks involved. in addition to these new instruments, we must be aware that the market is changing, globalizing very quickly and in the face of a globalized market, this evolution, with national supervisors, these instruments are in no way inappropriate and supervision ineffective. the growth of financial institutions also leads to a certain lack of monitoring of the place of this supervision and this supervision is also hampered at this point. what i meant by all this was that there is a lack of a truly holistic view of the sector, both geographically and in terms of its activities. understanding the interconnectedness of the players and the evolving nature of the business appears to be crucial to the security of the global financial system. i think that's what's been missing. the current basel rules are really about capital and i am pleased that the new arrangements implement the requirements related to liquidity aspects and countercyclical policy mechanisms. in the context of the poor performance of capital ratios as a proactive diagnostic measure of system stability, the attempt to standardise liquidity ratios in the short and long term should also be welcomed, since liquidity problems have actually forced the rescue measures of the banks we have observed.
in writing. the financial and economic crisis of recent years has removed the illusion that banks are the best at knowing their risks and setting their own security requirements. the gross ignorance of some bank managers, the prioritization of sales plans and the ignorance of risk factors, while the inaction of financial supervision, are the fundamental sins of the banking sector, which were the direct catalyst of the global recession. basel ii has proved to be a poorly effective mechanism for crisis prevention. in these circumstances, it is necessary to create a new basel iii code of standards as soon as possible, which no longer shares the optimistic assumption about the capacity of banks to self-regulate. the increase in capital requirements will certainly contribute to the safety of the banking sector through increased liquidity. however, such actions also carry the risk of passing costs on to bank customers, increasing the price of credit and other financial services to the detriment of the economy. it is therefore necessary to ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to prevent or at least minimise this unwanted phenomenon. on the other hand, we must also be aware that financial security comes at a cost. the question remains, how much are we willing to pay for them?
madam president! i would like to refer to the problems faced by mothers with small children and elderly people at european airports. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams in 2004 and 2005 was signed on the same day. unfortunately, the provisions of the regulation are not respected in most cases. even the highly successful tv advert commissioned by the european commission this year makes no mention of mothers or fathers travelling alone with small children. the solution is simple: effectively inform citizens of their rights. first, the title of the regulation should be amended to include the information that it also concerns mothers or fathers travelling alone with young children. secondly, a new pictogram for this group of passengers should be proposed, applicable at all airports in the member states of the european union.
madam president! the european union will have specific co2 emission limits from 2013. the european commission's recent plans to introduce a lower limit than previously planned, namely 0.688 tonnes of co2 per tonne of product produced, could lead to a disastrous situation for cement producers in many european countries, including poland. according to some media reports, such as the polish newspaper gazeta prawna, cement prices are expected to rise by at least 30%, which will hit a retail customer who wants to build a house or apartment, but will also hamper economic development wherever cement is the main means of production. this situation is particularly dangerous for new european countries that have a long way to go to catch up with rich countries such as france or germany, which have already built most of the infrastructure, such as motorways, long ago when there were no restrictions on this. and this situation also has this negative effect that some of the production will be moved beyond our eastern border and co2 will be produced and our economy will be lost.
madam president! in recent days, there have been reports of the deadly effects of the use of psychoactive substances, known as doping. this problem is also very evident in poland, where there is a growing wave of poisoning and even deaths, especially among young people. the ingenuity of manufacturers and sellers of additives wins out over the legislation of the member states. they are putting lethal drugs on the market long before states have the time to ban them by national law, and people who buy them are convinced that the doping, while not prohibited, is not harmful. nothing could be more wrong. cigarette burners are just as harmful as illegal drugs, and even more dangerous, because they are more addictive. in view of the very serious and growing social problem of doping, we must take decisive and effective action as soon as possible. the european commission, concerned about the health of thousands of young people, should urgently launch a large-scale information campaign on the harmfulness of doping and the risks associated with its use, and prepare new legal solutions.
author. − mr president, in the years to come, growth in europe will be supply-driven. sustainable and competitive investment patterns will be crucial. cohesion policy is a major source of european public investment and must work as a catalyst for structural change by investing in research and innovation, resource efficiency, new and sustainable jobs and infrastructure. it must not merely be a financial tool for investment. it is a policy that generates new resources, adding to growth potential. it will require an adequate macro-economic and financial framework to achieve its full impact. the key issue for post-2013 reform of cohesion policy is how to make it more effective in generating growth, jobs and competitiveness for the european economy in a sustainable way. social, economic and territorial cohesion is, according to the treaty, a basic principle of european integration. it must therefore be a policy applicable to all europe’s citizens, and not one restricted to the poorest regions. this is because it is not a subsidy policy based on the principle of compensation for the past, working as a supplement to national objectives, but rather a european policy for the future. it must take into account the post-crisis territorial reality at regional level, looking for the most effective solutions to the challenges and opportunities of different european territories. it must be made an integral part of the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy and its flagship initiatives. we are intensely aware of the necessity to ensure that cohesion policy and its cumulative effect over the whole territory of the union is one of the key instruments which will enable the union and its member states to achieve the ambitions of eu 2020. cohesion policy must contribute not only to reducing productivity gaps generated by the crisis, but also to putting productivity gains on track. it must invest in better links between leading regions and those that are catching up. it their development potential. in these exceptional times, we are convinced that they must all be encouraged and assisted to invest in ground-breaking ideas, in new technologies and in innovation. not to say pompously - as republic day. but i had then assumed the office of prime minister with the task of abolishing that state and leading the east germans to unity. at no time was there any other way of solving the open german question than in the context of european unification. with the european community, founded on the treaties of rome, the states had learned the right lessons from the horrors of two world wars. in 1957, chancellor konrad adenauer had the full membership of the east germans in the case of reunification enshrined in the treaties. the intention of the preamble to our constitution to 'act also for those who have been unable to cooperate' thus became practical policy. the german question has always been on the agenda, because it is also a key to overcoming the division of europe. the two are inextricably linked: the war that germany fought and lost, and the iron curtain that came down and divided europe. the tragedy was that it particularly affected the peoples who had already suffered most under national socialism. none of the subsequent uprisings could seriously shake communist rule, neither east berlin in 1953, nor the uprisings in poland and hungary in 1956, nor the prague spring of 1968. but from that moment on, it was known, it was known by many people in all the states of the eastern bloc, that the system in which we lived was probably not going to be reformed, but only overcome. this insight was something like a bleak hope, which could only be guarded against appearances and the behaviour of the powers, but which, in the opinion of most people - i was one of them - would remain unfulfilled in their lifetime. freedom was without voice, it was the time of oppressed speechlessness and paralysis. but that changed in october 1978 with the election of a pole as pope. he shook the regime of unfreedom with his faith and his word alone. first the poles, then the world felt that this man says what he believes and believes what he says. john paul ii was the first visible sign of the wind of change that was now blowing across europe and that was to become the storm of change in 1989. former president of the european commission. - mr president of the european parliament, mr prime minister lothar de maizière, mr president of the european council, mr president of the european commission, ladies and gentlemen, it is hardly a year since the fall of the berlin wall and the reunification of germany. throughout 1989 the peoples of europe were demonstrating: in poland, events all, we have to admit. some of us had a hunch about the growing imbalances in the communist countries, but no one could have foreseen that the pot would explode so quickly. this is a tremendous change in 1989, which, i remind you, saw the end of the pinochet dictatorship in chile and the tiananmen uprising in china, among other places on the planet. the events of 1989 could have triggered brutal repression, bloody conflicts, and a long period of instability and threat to peace at any time. it wasn't. this is the second lesson after the one we learned from the push of the people. we, the contemporaries of these events, have the duty to bear witness to them. the new generations must be educated about this period, for they have not lived through it. today they live in a world of prosperity and peace, yet they see the present world shaken by tension and revolt. so they have only a media image of violence and hatred. but they must bear in mind the overriding fact that, thanks to the wisdom of some world leaders in those years, 1989 and 1990, europeans were able to experience a transition, full of emotion, but without much bloodshed and without dangerous contamination. (applause) i will not mention the names of all those leaders - prime minister lothar de maizière did - whose calmness and wisdom i have just praised, and i fear i may forget or cause some sensitivity or be misunderstood. some of them, i should add, have unfortunately suffered the ingratitude of the peoples and their successors. history, i am sure, will correct these errors and omissions and deliver to us through these contributions the heart of the truth. but let us return to the shock of the fall of the berlin wall on november 9, 1989. even before politicians and diplomats could catch their breath, the european community had to react, if only by reference to the provision of the treaty of rome which mr lothar de maizière referred to. on 11 november, after having held an emergency meeting of the members of the european commission, i said on german television that the east germans were free to choose, but that they had their place in the european community. i added, and i quote, "we are a great community, within which we will build our destiny together to better control history, for the benefit of all". at the time, it was not possible to say more. my duty was to deliver a message of welcome and hope to our brothers in east germany, but at the same time i was trying to allay the fears and apprehensions of many, and this was not lacking. from then on, meetings between officials multiplied at world level, between the united states and the soviet union, between the latter and the europeans, or between the two germanys and the four allied powers of the last war, the so-called "2+4" process. at the same time, negotiations were progressing between the government of the federal republic of germany and the representatives of the gdr, and mainly between mr lothar de maizière and mr kohl. within the european community, many people wondered why they should hide it in the face of this radically new scene. but the european community could only approve and support the reunification of the two germanys, which it did at the european council in dublin on 24 april 1990. in doing so, and in taking note of the assurances given regarding the sustainability and fairness of the arrangements concluded at the level of the '2+4', the community was simply remaining faithful to the values which animate it: peace, mutual understanding between peoples, solidarity, and in particular with all germans, east and west. i am not sure that the existence of this community, and not merely its material prosperity, was always a reference point and an attraction for the peoples living under the communist yoke during the dark years. i would like to remind you that the community was in the throes of these events. as early as july 1989 - and roland dumas recalls, he was one of those players - the european commission had already got the g7 to accept a plan to help the countries of central and eastern europe, even before the wall fell. the spirit of openness and the willingness to accept enlargement had already been formally affirmed. but after the wall fell, the german question, why hide it, was the main concern. what fate was germany to choose? on 19 november 1989, at the initiative of françois mitterrand, an extraordinary european council met, which opened the way to regular consultation between the two germanys and their partners. a long speech by chancellor kohl gave an update on the situation, which, of course, could only be a turbulent one. the acceleration of history was well under way. the european parliament was also very active and attentive during this period. the debates reflected the questions raised by the future of germany and the risk, feared by many members, of a slowing down of the european integration effort stimulated by the single act treaty of 1987. on 28 november 1989 parliament adopted a very important resolution which states, and i quote: 'all the peoples of europe, including the polish people, have, in accordance with the helsinki final act, the right to live in the future within secure borders, as they are now defined.' the european parliament was referring to one of the most difficult debates, which ended with the maintenance of the oder-neisse frontier. it was before the european parliament on 17 january 1990 that i, as president of the european commission, confirmed, and i quote: 'east germany is a special case. it has its place in the community if it so wishes.' in view of these prospects, your parliament is setting up a temporary committee to study the impact of the process of german reunification on the european community. this committee, composed - i should stress - of highly experienced personalities - several foreign ministers - made an effective contribution to removing doubts and preparing the integration of the eastern länder. we should remind the sceptics of all sides that, thanks to the european parliament, pluralistic and living democracy is not a vain concept but a reality. she showed it on that occasion. (applause) in sum, whatever difficulties the construction of europe has to overcome, it is wrong to underestimate its achievements and influence. i shall not, of course, venture to establish a hierarchy of ideas and facts which may have influenced this great liberation movement. perhaps the most important remains the ability of peoples to resist oppression, to express their desire for freedom, to demonstrate their quiet courage. but i would not like to ignore the appeals of john paul ii, and in particular his crucial words to the poles: "do not be afraid!" i also remember the firm, open and generous policy of west germany towards the gdr in the years before the fall of the wall. a moment when freedom triumphs, but freedom has its demands. the german reunification treaty presented a twofold challenge. firstly, the question of understanding between west and east germans, which was raised with great lucidity, understanding and generosity. then there was the economic and social challenge, which was equally difficult. an exceptional effort was made by the massive transfer of resources from the west to the east, of the order of 4 to 5% of west germany's national product each year, or, ladies and gentlemen, 1 400 billion euros over 20 years, not to mention other contributions in the form of technical assistance, to restructure the economy of the east. to illustrate the results by a single figure, it should be noted that in 20 years the per capita income of the east of germany has risen from 40 to 73% of the income of the west. the effort will be continued in the coming years by maintaining the solidarity tax if i understand correctly, until 2019. the germans themselves agree. there is still work to be done in terms of attitudes and economic and social structures. the european community has also made the eastern länder benefit from the economic and social cohesion policy, which is well known to parliamentarians. even if the sums committed are not of the order of magnitude of the effort made by the germans, the european contributions were a sign of the east germans' full and complete membership of the european venture, the multiplication of human and technical exchanges, the regular dialogue between the european commission and the leaders of the new länder. i would have liked the commission to do more, but the german authorities, concerned about the reactions of their partners, asked me not to go any further in the effort provided by the structural funds. ladies and gentlemen, twenty years later, when the european adventure is raising many questions beyond the financial crisis, the 27 countries are faced with a historic responsibility: to deepen european integration or to live day by day through compromises, which are necessary but do not carry any future. (applause) i would like to thank on this day when we are celebrating the german reunification, how can we not question the country's vision for the future of europe? the unified germany is the strongest economic power of the 27 countries that make up the union. to cite just one figure, it represents 25% of the gdp of the economic and monetary union. i quote it because, whether we like it or not, it is the strongest link between the european countries which share the same currency with the rights, but also with the duties that this entails. many in europe would tend to forget that. (applause) i would like to thank germany is now geopolitically situated at the crossroads of the european union and the rest of the european continent. it is a strong position, attractive in some respects, which raises many questions in germany as in other countries. the germans themselves agree with this, as is shown by their white paper on security in germany. i quote: 'given its size, its demographic weight, its economic strength and its geographical position in the heart of the continent, a united germany must play an important role in shaping the european project of tomorrow and beyond.' the period before 1989 is therefore no longer relevant, when germany was showing restraint and delicacy, for reasons that everyone could understand and even appreciate. this restraint led successive german governments to take the lead in european integration, particularly when it came to abandoning the powerful dm - i mean the powerful dm, because it is 10 marks - symbol of the german renaissance, in favour of the euro, the single currency. i am not speaking out of nostalgia, but as one of europe's activists, who today addresses germany, whose reunification we are celebrating, but which is valid for all the member states. are the values which the founding fathers of europe have bequeathed to us still present and dominant? the legacy that has been handed down to us is more about 'why do we want to live together?' than treaties, necessary institutional arrangements. but i would not like to end on this necessary questioning, this little pessimism that runs. no, you can't! i have deep memories and a special fondness for the night of 3 october, when we had the honour and the joy - enrique báron, president of the european parliament, and i - of being invited to this memorable evening in the old reichstag. the german leaders of west and east germany were united in a fervent communion, an atmosphere of seriousness and happiness. all europeans would have shared this great emotion. after the ceremony, i wanted to walk through the streets of berlin and feel the feelings of a people. there was also nothing but seriousness and joy, no exuberance, no ostentatious display. a quiet night that everyone enjoyed thinking of past ruptures, the anguish of families divided by a decree of history. i was thinking of this europe free of hatred and conflict, a europe which i wanted to see united, strong and generous at the same time. and you will agree that there is still much to be done to consolidate the acquis and move forward into the future. in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased to welcome the positive outcome of today's vote in the european parliament on visa liberalisation for the western balkan countries. following the lifting of the visa requirement for citizens of serbia, montenegro and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia in december 2009, it was expected that relevant decisions would be taken in relation to bosnia and herzegovina and albania. the opening up of the european union to more balkan peoples will have many positive effects for all concerned. first, it is an unprecedented convenience for ordinary citizens, who can now see firsthand what the european union looks like and travel freely throughout the member states. secondly, it is another very important step aimed at stabilising the situation in the region and creating a positive climate for further reforms and the future integration of all balkan countries into the european union. however, in parallel, appropriate decisions should be taken on the visa requirements for citizens of kosovo. the people of this country should not remain the only completely isolated nation in the balkans, and the privileges of free travel in europe should extend to this country as well. i am very pleased with the initiative taken by the european parliament to lift the visa regime for bosnia and herzegovina and albania. this is the next step in the integration of the balkan countries into the european area, which i strongly support.
in writing. - i fully support the proposal prepared by the european parliament and the council to lift the requirement for short-stay visas for citizens of albania and bosnia and herzegovina when crossing the external borders. these countries have made good progress in adapting to the requirements of the european union. the commission has proposed that, once the visa requirement has been lifted, it will appropriately monitor in those two countries and in all western balkan countries which have already moved from a 'negative list' to a 'positive list' the process of effective and sustained implementation of the measures envisaged by those countries in the framework of visa liberalisation. the commission also stresses that the basic condition for the completion of the visa liberalisation process in these countries is the introduction of biometric passports, which will guarantee security and prevent illegal migration.

in writing. - the death penalty is the most cruel and inhuman punishment. it is a violation of the most fundamental of human rights - the right to life. that is why i believe that the abolition of the death penalty is one of the european union's priorities in promoting democracy and human rights in the world. in europe, the prohibition of the death penalty is a strong value, guaranteed by protocols 6 and 13 of the european convention on human rights. the european union is totally opposed to the use of the death penalty - whatever the circumstances. eu action in this field is a top priority of its external human rights policy. the eu has consistently called for the abolition of the death penalty worldwide and is therefore the largest financial supporter of civil society organisations working for the abolition of the death penalty. under the european instrument for democracy and human rights, more than €15 million has been allocated to support such projects since 1994.
in writing. the natural disaster in the gulf of mexico caused by the deepwater oil spill is a good moment to consider a european action plan to prevent similar events. the unimaginable damage that the spill has done to the gulf of mexico ecosystem and the southern coast of the united states should be a powerful incentive for us to act. first, the union must increase its capacity to respond rapidly to such disasters. an appropriate system of coordination of national services should be provided to increase the effectiveness of the fight against spills and the remediation of damage. secondly, there is a need to strengthen the safety control of existing and newly built installations. the process of licensing oil extraction and leasing facilities to third parties should be better monitored. thirdly, there is a need to create an appropriate legal framework governing liability and redress of possible damages, as there are a number of significant legal loopholes in the current legislation. it is also worth considering the creation of a compensation fund to finance the crisis response in such situations.
in writing. − the european union is concerned about the rapid rate of biodiversity loss and the failure to meet the global biodiversity target for 2010 of significantly reducing the rate of biodiversity loss. in order to achieve ambitious targets, specific and evidence-based indicators for assessing progress towards the strategic objectives should be defined as soon as possible. studies to date estimate the decline in quality of life due to loss of diversity at €50 billion per year (just under 1% of gdp), with a projected increase to €14 trillion in 2050. the european union therefore considers this problem to be of the utmost urgency. i support the belief that there are many links between climate protection and the achievement of the millennium development goals and the reduction of biodiversity loss. actions to protect biodiversity have a positive impact on climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies. i agree with the call in the resolution to support efforts to strengthen the synergies and links between biodiversity and climate policy. however, to help prevent these global problems, a radical increase in global funds for biodiversity conservation is needed, particularly through existing sources of funding as well as through new, innovative sources, including new and innovative market instruments.
in writing. - biodiversity affects the lives of all of us. however, man's activities have accelerated the rate at which the earth is being lost. the effects of climate change include avalanche deforestation, declining fish stocks, and the disappearance of species. scientists estimate that between 15 and 40 percent of them could disappear by the end of the 21st century. it is worthwhile to realize that the loss of biodiversity negatively affects the activities of ecosystems and the services they provide, such as food supply, water purification, soil fertilization, flood protection and energy production. biodiversity is threatened by many factors, such as climate change, uncontrolled urban sprawl, and invasive alien species. but i'd like to focus on one specific issue. it's agriculture, which is often cited as one of the threats to biodiversity. surely it can be said that industrial agriculture is not good for the environment. but i think the far greater environmental risk is that we're going to abandon agriculture. we've seen a lot of this happening lately. the declining profitability of agricultural production, caused by, among other things, price fluctuations, is driving people away from farming, leading to the disappearance of life in large areas.
in writing. − the draft resolution on the european union's cohesion and regional policy after 2013 is a clear signal from the european parliament to the european commission on the minimum requirements for policy-making in the future programming period. the aim of cohesion policy is to reduce disparities in the level of development of european regions and to increase the growth potential for achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion. cohesion policy, as a sign of european solidarity, plays a very important role in the europe 2020 agenda. its effective implementation is essential for further modernisation and for ensuring sustainable, stable economic growth and job creation in europe. it is designed to increase competitiveness and improve the quality of life of eu citizens. i am firmly in favour of rejecting any attempt to renationalize cohesion policy and to divide it into sectors, to disperse the resources of this policy across sectors. it is worth noting the need for multi-level governance, the importance of working with the regions to make cohesion policy as user-friendly as possible and the need to better coordinate rural development with cohesion development objectives.

rapporteurs as well to the committee on legal affairs and the committee on foreign affairs who have worked hard and constructively during the whole process. last but not least, allow me to express my gratitude to cathy, her team and the commission services for their enormously hard work which will lead, i hope, to the establishment of the eeas in a very short period of time. this week’s work will conclude the complex work of laying the legal and budgetary foundation for the eeas. they build on and are fully in line with the cornerstone of this process – the eeas decision. i had the privilege of participating in the discussion on setting up the eeas and i was honoured to represent the commission in the famous quadrilogue in madrid. i can be a direct witness as to how important the contribution of the representatives of the european parliament, mr brok, mr verhofstadt and mr gualtieri was to the successful conclusion of our very intense debate on this matter. i think the input they brought to our debate really contributed to having the eeas as a truly efficient and effective european diplomatic service. the same can be said about the work of your rapporteur, mr rapkay. the amendments to the staff regulations appear to be of a purely administrative nature, but they are not. they are essential in enabling the service to be up and running and to truly serve european interests. the commission is of the opinion that the compromise package tabled by your rapporteur, mr rapkay, is a very good result that can be fully supported. the amendments have led, in my view, to a real improvement of the whole text. let me highlight just a couple of the core elements of the proposal. as you know, the eeas will be composed in its starting phase of the three sources mentioned in the treaty, namely the commission, the council general secretariat and national diplomats. the relevant departments of the council and the commission will be transferred to the eeas, while the existing rights of the staff working in these departments will be fully guaranteed. national diplomats will be able to apply for published vacant posts. i am happy to say that, as of 1 july 2013, officials from other institutions including the european parliament, will also be able to apply to the eeas on an equal footing. permanent officials and national diplomats will have the same rights and obligations in the eeas and the necessary provisions of the staff regulations will apply to ensure their independence and loyalty to the european union. national diplomats will have contracts which can last up to a maximum of ten years. in addition, member states will provide national diplomats with a guarantee of immediate reinstatement after their service in the european external action service. the compromise also includes provisions which express a strong commitment to reaching geographical and gender balance in the european external action service. the situation will be reviewed in 2013 with a report by the high representative to be presented to the european parliament, the council and the commission. i know that some of you in this house would have wished for stronger provisions in these proposals, whereas others were vehemently opposed. i am convinced that the amendments, as tabled to you now, constitute a balanced solutions. the negotiations on this file have not always been easy. the preparatory process was quite complex as it required a consultation with our staff representative, but the hard work and the intensive negotiations have paid off, and you have a very good negotiation result for your house on your desks. i therefore hope that the european parliament will adopt these amendments tomorrow. allow me to conclude by expressing the commission’s strong commitment to ensuring the smooth creation of the eeas and its readiness to provide all necessary support and help to this new european service. i hope that tomorrow will mark a historic vote by this house which will lead to the establishment of the european external action service.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. − mr president, my committee, the committee on foreign affairs, pronounced itself in favour of a strong eeas by an overwhelming majority. ‘strong’ means subject to democratic and parliamentary scrutiny and control. ‘strong’ means communautaire – i.e. representing the community of all 27 member states, respecting the geographical dimension and diversity of the union of today, and not of yesterday. half a year ago geographical balance was not an issue. today it is, and will remain so, and paragraph 7 of our resolution and article 6(6) will point this out. two hundred meps from the new member states in this house will also be keeping an eye on this. far more emphasis was placed on geographical balance than was the case in the initial proposal, although this was not sufficient. arithmetic is not always right, and laws and geography cannot be outvoted. we believe that all men and women are equal and not that some are more equal than others. this also applies to the foreign service of the union. lady ashton, we look forward to your actions to correct the present discrimination against new member states in what will become the eeas.
author of the draft opinion of the committee on development. - the opinion of the committee on development on the staff regulations was adopted unanimously. the committee on development supports the amendments proposed in the draft report of the legal affairs committee, in particular those aimed at ensuring that recruitment of staff for the european external action service is based on objective and transparent procedures laid down in the staff regulations and the conditions of employment of other servants of the communities. in addition, the commission proposal improves on the amendments proposed by the rapporteur-general, mr rapkay, introducing provisions on the staff of the european external action service, which were incorporated in the political agreement. they concern in particular gender and geographical balance among staff and balance between staff from the institutions of the european union and staff from national diplomatic services. i hope that the new external action service will appreciate the autonomous nature of development cooperation and not treat it as a 'marche card', as an instrument of foreign policy. this was the main objective of the development committee's work.
on behalf of the ppe group. i am sure that no one in this house has the slightest doubt about how important the european external action service will be to the functioning of the community. our work over the past months has focused on ensuring that the service has the right legal basis and the appropriate instruments for future effective operation. we worked under time pressure, and negotiations were often difficult. we have reached agreement with the council and the commission on a number of issues and i hope that the compromises reached will lead to a positive final result. the legal affairs committee was tasked with proposing changes to the staff regulations that would suit the needs of the new service while guaranteeing its independence and high level of content. i think the amendments voted on yesterday evening by the legal affairs committee provide such guarantees, although i am not entirely satisfied with them, particularly on one point. i think that the question of geographical balance, which has been raised so often, could have been resolved in a much better way. i am of course pleased with the declarations by the high representative that she will pay particular attention to ensuring the participation of citizens of all member states in the service, and that a report will be produced in 2013 in which she will provide information on the work of the service. the eu's diplomacy is supposed to be european, and it is true that the nationality of its staff should not play a particular role. however, where we come from, what our roots are, shapes our worldview, which in turn has a significant impact on how we see the world around us. if europe is to be united in diversity, it must be given the chance to ensure that this diversity is properly preserved and reflected. and that is what our discussions on geographical balance were about, not, as some people wrongly think and misinterpret, the provision of fixed amounts to the member states. i thank the rapporteurs for their good cooperation and i hope that mrs ashton will put our work to good use in her work.
on behalf of the ecr group. the union is a union of 27 countries and this fact should be reflected in the structure of the institution that is to represent the european union in the outside world. the impression should not be given that some countries are not treated subjectively in connection with the creation of a new service. the service should reflect the richness of culture and the different national traditions in europe, including in the area of diplomacy. that is why, together with a group of members, we have prepared an amendment which introduces a geographical balance factor. the idea is that, with similar qualifications, the geographical criteria should be the deciding factor in the selection of candidates. it is not a solution that rigidly imposes such geographical criteria on the recruitment of future staff, but one that is flexible and applied in a supplementary way. the adoption of such a record will eliminate the existing disparities and will allow for greater representativeness over time. i would like to emphasise that this solution retains the primary importance of the competence criterion, which is so important for the creators of these solutions.
ladies and gentlemen! in discussing the shape of the external action service, we cannot ignore or marginalise the issue of maintaining an appropriate geographical balance among the staff. at present, the number of workers from the old 15 member states significantly and disproportionately exceeds the number of workers from the new member states. i'll give you a few figures: until the last appointments, only two of the 115 ambassadors were from countries that joined the union after 2004. of the 29 ambassadors recently appointed, only four are from the new member states. we cannot allow this division to become the rule of the future external action service. without adequate geographical representation, we are unable to create a strong and effective external action service that works in the interests of all of us. and we will not be proud of the service that the high representative, lady ashton, has spoken of. i am also convinced that the application of a transitional period during which the disproportionately low representation of the new member states would be gradually levelled out will allow us to reach a state of affairs in which our objective of promoting the european union as a key player in the international arena can be achieved in an efficient and effective manner.
we regret that the demands of the majority of members of the committee on foreign affairs for a balanced geographical representation in the newly formed external action service of the union are facing serious problems and even strong resistance. the difficulties in developing the rules for the recruitment of staff in eu diplomatic missions are also apparent. the principle of solidarity and representativeness, which has long been a hallmark of the union, must not be eclipsed by the selfishness of some large member states. the diplomatic missions chapter is under the jurisdiction of the lady catherine ashton here today, who grants them solely on a discretionary basis. of the several dozen diplomatic missions around the world, the sixth largest country in the european union, poland, receives only two. it is therefore worth asking what criteria the commissioner used to make this distinction. i would like to remind you that it is our house that decides on the budget of the eu diplomacy.
today marks the end of a very special procedure, the procedure for the creation of a new european institution. i represent the new member states and i've been fascinated to see what integration looks like in practice, what these push-ups between the different institutions look like, how something is finally being born that is supposed to consolidate what is so lacking in the european union, namely a common foreign policy. and it worked, parliament was involved. i'm very proud that we were active. it is a service of the whole european union, not just of one institution. but also this integration was about integrating new countries with old ones. let's just say i did half-way on this test. if there are questions and doubts today, it is because the commissioner, the vice-president of the council, must ensure that all staffing decisions are transparent and show that the best people are given jobs. then i won't fight for geographical parity, because for me, the parity of wisdom and qualifications is much more important than the parity of geography, but you have to prove it. in writing. the report by bernhard rapkay on the changes to the staff regulations in the context of the creation of the european external action service (eeas) is a very important document for the development of the union's foreign policy. the bone of contention in the final days before the report was adopted was the issue of 'geographical balance'. meps from the so-called old countries argued that the eu diplomacy that was being created should recruit the 'best of the best' and be based only on the knowledge and experience of the candidates ('merit only'), while meps from the 'new' countries pointed out that there was no shortage of excellent professionals in our countries either, but despite the passage of 6 years since the accession of the 10 new countries, it is still strongly underrepresented in eu structures. for example, the share of poles in the european commission's directorate-general for relex, which will be integrated into the eeas, is only 2%. the concept of 'geographical balance' as proposed by the rapporteur is, in my view, vague and cannot constitute a clear legal basis for measures to correct this imbalance. i am therefore unable to support the report, although it contains many valuable proposals beyond this point.
, in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that the regulations on the european external action service, if properly structured, will ensure its effective and efficient functioning. building such a comprehensive body dealing with an important and growing area of the european union's work is a challenge in today's global reality. in particular, i am keen to see the service strengthen europe's position by carrying out its activities. to this end, it should be ensured that it is composed of highly qualified people with the appropriate skills and experience, so that representatives from each member state can participate in the implementation of the union's foreign policy. i am pleased that the text of mr rapkaya's report takes into account issues such as promoting equal opportunities for the under-represented sex in certain functional groups and geographical balance in the recruitment of eeas staff. a well-organised service, with the best experts from all the member states, is an opportunity for the european union to become even more relevant and to realise its full potential on the international stage.
we are holding a debate on poverty during the european year against poverty and social exclusion. it is important that our efforts, as well as those of governments and ngos, are permanent and not just about action and propaganda. of all the measures proposed in this report, the requirement of a minimum income in relation to the average wage is of particular importance. the causes of poverty are diverse, often linked to pathology and social exclusion. but what is particularly striking and very shameful is the fact that poverty exists among working people, even those with no children or only a small number of children. this is unacceptable and the action of the european commission and parliament must therefore be extremely effective, consistent and decisive. by helping people on different continents and by providing humanitarian aid in the event of natural disasters, we should first of all set an example of solidarity with citizens affected by poverty in the european union.
in writing. dear colleagues, according to statistics, 16% of eu citizens are affected by poverty. one of the main reasons for the increase in the number of poor people in the eu member states is the lack of adequate education and skills adapted to the requirements of the labour market. poverty is also associated with great emotional stress, fear, stress, and lack of choice. these factors make it very common for people who are poor to face another problem, which is social exclusion. children from poor families are denied the opportunities that children from better-off families have. a young person growing up in such an environment has neither the opportunities nor the appropriate role models to escape the cycle of poverty in the future. the year 2010 has been declared the european year for combating poverty and social exclusion. we therefore have a unique opportunity to raise awareness of the problems of the poor and the excluded in the international community and to suggest concrete solutions.
in writing. poverty and social exclusion are a violation of human dignity and fundamental rights. the main objective of income support programmes should be to lift people out of poverty and enable them to live in dignity. the latest statistics are alarming. there are 1.4 billion people in the world and about 85 million people in the european union currently live in poverty. the european parliament and the member states should take further action to increase the number and quality of jobs and wages, and to guarantee fair pensions, pensions and family allowances. it is necessary to ensure universal access to high-quality public services. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. at present, the minimum wage in poland is about 42% of the average wage. raising it would help lift adults and older people out of poverty, give them the right to a decent life, and give every child a chance to grow and get an education. in particular, the last issue, education, requires effective action, in particular against the factors that contribute to early school leaving and to improve the level of vocational qualifications. i believe that the basis for implementing concrete actions and policies to increase access to education for young people should be created, for example through scholarships and student loans and grants.
in writing. 2010 is the eu's year to fight poverty and social exclusion. one in six europeans, or 17 per cent of the population, lives below the poverty line. in poland, that's about 6.5 million people. poverty can affect anyone. all you have to do is lose your job, get seriously ill. increasingly, working people are joining the ranks of the poor. the poverty that most affects children and the elderly, young people, mental workers, graduates, large families, people who are paying off loans. it is the duty of parliament to tackle and combat the causes of poverty effectively. our goal is to reduce the number of poor by 20 million by 2020. ensuring adequate material support for the poor, facilitating access to the labour market and educational opportunities, and ensuring high quality public services for all should be at the forefront of national poverty reduction strategies. social and ethical issues are equally important. poverty is also a state of mind that involves a loss of dignity and humiliation. and changing that mindset is one of the hardest things about fighting poverty. what we need here is effective psychological care and speed in delivering help. national strategies should be consistent with initiatives supported by the european social fund and projects under the community progress programme. may 2010 be an opportunity for social dialogue to promote the ratification of the european social charter by all eu countries.

the control of vessels engaged in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is necessary and should be carried out efficiently, effectively and as often as possible, with particular attention to the areas where the risk of poaching is highest. that is why we need the new control measures introduced by the regulation so badly. the control systems applied by regional fisheries organisations should be transposed into community law in such a way as to avoid delays and legal loopholes resulting from complex procedures. i also agree with the author that the justification of delays by lack of human resources is unacceptable.
the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the northwest atlantic fisheries is primarily concerned with the optimal management of fisheries resources in the areas covered by the agreement. it should be borne in mind that the convention aims at a broad international cooperation, using scientific research, to make the management of marine resources as efficient as possible. the main changes to the convention concern the modernisation of its organisation, the reform of the system of contributions to the budget, the redefinition of the responsibilities of the parties and the reform of the dispute settlement procedure. i agree with the rapporteur and believe that these changes will be beneficial to the interests of the european union, which is authorised to fish in these areas by virtue of the convention.
in writing. − the report proposes a number of amendments to bring the rules on the regulatory and control procedure into line with the new rules on delegated acts introduced by the lisbon treaty. the rapporteur's aim was to amend the eu directive on the collection of data by type of goods for maritime transport statistics. currently, 18 member states collect this data on a voluntary basis. five member states do not have a sea coast and therefore do not provide the data required by this directive. it is worth emphasising that the collection of data does not impose any additional burden on respondents, as the member states concerned have them and are able to provide them using existing data sources, such as customs documents. the collection of data by type of goods is mandatory in european statistics on road, rail and inland waterway transport. given the need to create efficient and coordinated green transport networks (maritime, land and inland), it is highly desirable to collect and analyse data from all modes of transport.
in writing. - the report refers to the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic, which entered into force on 17 march 1982. the neafc was set up to monitor the recommendations agreed in this document. the report stressed the importance of adopting appropriate measures to control and enforce the rules applicable to all fishing vessels engaged in or intended to engage in fishing activities for fishery resources in the convention area. the key issue is the coverage of this area by measures to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, which are implemented by regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo). it is therefore a priority to change the control and enforcement system adopted by neafc, which should be transposed into eu legislation as soon as possible. the rapporteur also stresses the importance of eu fishing vessels being required to have authorisations to fish outside eu waters. this report will fill the existing legal gaps in the eu fleet legislation and thus increase the credibility of the european union in this area and help to combat illegal fishing.
in writing. - the report by mr jarosław wałęsa refers to the amendment to the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the northwest atlantic fisheries, which was signed in ottawa on 24 october 1978 and entered into force on 1 january 1979. nafo, or the northwest atlantic fisheries organisation, is responsible for the rational management, use and protection of fisheries resources through consultation and cooperation. the main responsibility of this organisation is to promote international cooperation to improve the sustainable management of marine resources on the high seas, based on the basic principles of scientific research. the rapporteur is making favourable amendments to the convention to bring the existing rules more into line with instruments at international and regional level. the proposed changes include: modernising the structure of nafo (merging the general council and the fisheries commission into one body), reforming the system of contributions to the budget, creating clear guidelines on the rights and obligations of contracting parties belonging to nafo, changes to the decision-making process and introducing a new dispute settlement procedure that will allow for a smooth resolution of disputes in the interests of the european union.
in writing. - women's career paths are often burdened by the stereotype that they are weaker, less resilient, more likely to become pregnant and therefore to take more sick leave than men. this also makes it harder for women to find jobs, and those who do are paid less than their male counterparts in the same positions. the economic crisis has highlighted these problems and shown how women are exploited in the labour market. short-term contracts, part-time contracts, unpaid overtime are just a few examples of what i find unacceptable. it is therefore necessary to pay attention to the observance of labour law on an equal basis with all employees. the exploitation of people's hardship to force them to work in unhealthy and unpleasant conditions must be counteracted, especially when it comes to women, who have to deal with additional stereotypes.
in writing. − the rapporteur understands 'uncertain work' as employment which is characterised by low job security, low pay, lack of social protection and employment benefits, lack of protection against discrimination, limited opportunities for promotion on the labour market, collective representation of workers and a work environment which does not meet minimum safety and health standards. the financial and economic crisis has made the problem of precarious work even more visible and urgent. the entrepreneurs have drastically reduced temporary employment and there is a fear that the jobs lost will not be restored. unfortunately, the situation affects women the most and is most visible in the service sector (hotel, catering, education, health, social work) and in agriculture. women work part-time in these sectors, resulting in lower wages and pensions, less social support and no promotion opportunities. recent studies show that women's ability to get a job is much lower than men's. moreover, there is still a huge gender pay gap (around 18%, with women earning one fifth less per hour than men). in view of the above problems, i voted in favour of the report proposing a solution to this difficult employment situation.
in writing. - i supported the report on women in precarious employment. the economic crisis has destabilised the labour market. employers have reduced employment or hired temporary workers with worse financial conditions. the wave of layoffs has also left many people out of the job market. graduates, the elderly, and women were particularly affected. the crisis has exacerbated existing gender employment disparities. this has been particularly felt by women, who represent the largest proportion of workers in so-called precarious employment. the financial gap in earnings has widened, and inequalities in social protection have increased. this situation has also hampered the professional development of women and contributed to the perpetuation of gender stereotypes in the workplace. women in so-called precarious employment should therefore be given special protection! they should be covered by, inter alia, social security schemes and employment protection legislation. it is also important to provide financial security for women in the event of unemployment or maternity. women in precarious employment should also be able to benefit from trade union protection. in addition, women working exclusively in the home should be guaranteed free access to social rights counselling services. i also draw attention to the need to regulate the legal situation of seasonal workers, who are more exposed to various irregularities because of the nature of their work.
the rapporteur. - today we are meeting to discuss the 2011 budget of the european union. 2011 is a special budget year for several reasons. first of all, this is already the fifth year of the 2007-13 multiannual financial perspective, so we already know a lot about how this multiannual financial perspective is being implemented, what has gone well, what has not, and many programmes are already well advanced in terms of their so-called life cycle. meanwhile, a lot has happened in the european union. we have adopted the treaty of lisbon, which imposes or defines new areas of action for the european union. i would like to mention a few, especially those which are costly, namely the new areas of action in the framework of the policy to combat climate change, in the framework of the energy policy; it opens up new areas of action for the european union on the global stage, i.e. the emergence of eu diplomacy; new activities in the field of space exploration, sport, tourism. all these new tasks are not, unfortunately, adequately funded. it is a bit like the european union has new ambitions, new plans, but not necessarily new material means to implement them. and that's what 2011 is. in its draft, the european parliament believes that the european commission has reasonably planned the actions and the corresponding measures for 2011. the council - as we have discussed here before - has reduced these measures. i would like to briefly present what happened in the committee on budgets during our reading. as a reminder, the new lisbon treaty also introduces a new budgetary procedure. we don't have two chances now. neither the council nor the european parliament have two readings anymore. we only have one reading, which means that both arms of the budgetary authority need to be extra disciplined and extra hard, because we only get one chance at each of these things. i repeat, we are no longer on two readings. we're voting tomorrow, we're going to lean on the position of the budget committee. it is important to emphasize that the position adopted by the committee on budgets respects the multiannual financial perspective. unlike in previous years, the european parliament will adopt its own reading, which does not go beyond the multiannual financial perspective in terms of the amounts planned. it is a position that is as innovative as it is one that takes into account and takes into account the concerns and the situation in which the council finds itself. the situation in which seven member states rejected the council's position was not lost on the european parliament. we listen to and take into account the concerns of some member states and the council as such. we have read the council's position carefully and that is why our reading as the european parliament is disciplined and does not go beyond the multiannual financial framework. on the other hand, we cannot of course remain indifferent to the fact, as i said earlier, that we have new areas for the european union to deal with and there are no adequate financial guarantees for them. moreover, the council has committed itself to a large number of measures, such as those relating to bananas, compensation for banana producers, the iter programme and others, which require new funding and for which there is no new funding. they're supposed to be funded by the people in attendance. and here, as the european parliament, we have our doubts. what we would also like to communicate in our reading is, first of all, to emphasise once again the priority triangle, the triangle of youth, education and mobility. since march, as the european parliament, we have been informing that this will be our set of priorities for 2011 and we would like those budget lines that favour youth, education and mobility to be appropriately funded, so that there are also funds for novel, innovative projects on youth mobility and education. the same applies to research and innovation programmes. we know that there are not enough funds in the current financial perspective, and that is why we have made the painful but in our opinion necessary cuts to the iter programme. i would very much like this reading of parliament to be seen as a disciplined reading, but at the same time a reading that allows the european union to finance its commitments for 2011.
the committee on budgetary control considers that the following points should be noted. the first is the level of errors that occur during budgeting and implementation. the two areas of particular importance are external action and the structural funds. another thing that is crucial for us is the amounts that are allocated in the traditional way, on the basis of a ratio based on the evaluation of the effects of the measures used. this is the second aspect that we often miss when we make budgetary decisions. the third area is the harmonised budget, for example the cohesion fund, the transeuropean transport networks. it seems that we are using too little european methodology in budgeting and too much national fragmentation. the last budgetary element is a request to take account of the fact that national reports on the implementation of budgetary commitments in the past year are included. so far, less than half of the countries have submitted them, using a very different methodology.

we are talking about a new budget for the european union in the context of the crisis of public finances in many member states, in the context of very serious cuts in national budgets, so it is not surprising that we are also looking for these cuts in the eu budget. i would just like to draw attention to the fact that the most effective, the most powerful anti-crisis instrument we have in our hands is the common market. the balanced common market can be achieved more quickly through cohesion investments, structural investments. so do not look for cuts where we are dealing with neither social aid nor money-eating policies, but with investments that help to reap all the benefits of the common market, which we extended in 2004 and 2007. and one more thing. today we're talking about this new budget in the context of building diplomatic institutions. do not expect central european meps to unconditionally support an increase in external service expenditure when their interests and their countries are not equally represented in these new institutions.

mr president, i would like to congratulate you on the excellent job you did today. i really appreciate the way you exercised your chairmanship today, and i hope you will share your wonderful skills with other vice-chairs of parliament.
in writing. - the entry into force of the lisbon treaty has given new powers to both the european commission and the european parliament. the draft revised text of the framework agreement reflects the effective implementation of the treaty changes in the relationship between the institutions. it makes favourable changes in the legislative procedure, parliamentary scrutiny and the obligation to provide information. it is a significant step forward in relations with the commission and a major step towards closer cooperation. the exchange of information and constructive dialogue allows us to achieve more effective and transparent results, which is key from the point of view of the eu citizens whose interests we represent. i therefore consider the agreement to give priority to the participation of ec members in plenary sessions and other meetings related to the ep's activities to be very important. in particular, i am pleased that the commission is committed to working closely with the ep on proposals for citizens' legislative initiatives at an early stage. this allows us to stay closer to our citizens in the ep, which raises the quality of our democracy. however, in order to act effectively in the interests of eu citizens, the commission should grant meps observer status at all international conferences, make it even easier for us to attend other important meetings where possible, and keep the ep informed of the negotiating positions adopted by the commission at such meetings and conferences.
in writing. - we are nearing the end of the tumultuous work on the shape of the european external action service, which today's vote brings us closer to achieving. we talk a lot about sustainability in terms of gender, geography, we point to the transparency of recruitment based on known principles and rules, but the most important thing is the quality and effectiveness of the sdh, which is why the substantive criteria related to staff recruitment are so important. i would like to point out the need, indeed the necessity, for the involvement of people from the relevant directorates-general of the european commission, as well as the council of the eu and the parliament. this is not about representing the eu institutions, but about preparing these people in the various areas of the union's activities, such as the difficult issues of energy, trade, agriculture, not to mention human rights and terrorism. i fear that there is a large proportion of people in this service with a general knowledge of diplomacy but no knowledge of the complex issues involved.
in writing. - abstaining is not the answer. the absent are wrong. i think there are many more good solutions in the resolution than there are less good ones. we need the european external action service. it should act as soon as possible to increase europe's standing in the world. the resolution adopted says that all member countries will be represented in the service. now we have to make sure that it actually happens. it gives credence to the process of setting up the external action service. it should be remembered that the european union was built on mutual trust, which poland benefits from. i'll be watching this trial very closely.

in writing. - i am very pleased to congratulate the rapporteur, ms sidonia jędrzewska, on her excellent report. we have adopted today for the first time a community budget based on the provisions of the treaty of lisbon and for the first time we have not exceeded the financial framework set by the current financial perspective. i believe that the solutions proposed by ms sidonia yedriyevskaya are a realistic and pragmatic approach in a difficult time of economic crisis. i am also pleased to note that the budget adopted today provides financial support for the european parliament's priorities.
in writing. − in the face of an ageing population and the difficulties facing the european economy, all opportunities must be used to encourage women to have children, but also to make it easier for them to return to work. many women are outstanding professionals in their fields, and the european economy cannot afford not to benefit from the services of highly qualified workers. the same is true of women living and working in rural areas. often they do not have full maternity leave and must return to work quickly. this, of course, is a danger to both their health and that of the baby. these women should therefore be entitled to the same privileges as women working outside agriculture.
in writing. - i would like to emphasise that in mrs edite estreli's report i voted for the provisions on 20 weeks' maternity leave, for the protection of women against unjustified dismissal for 6 months after returning from maternity leave and for full pay, the protection of women during breastfeeding, but in this case without any specific solutions, because i believe that the definition of these provisions should be left to the member states. in the case of multiple births, i think that leave should be extended accordingly. i always support all solutions that allow women to be safe mothers and guarantee better conditions for their return to the labour market.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a report on the health safety of pregnant women and those on maternity leave. by adopting this common position, we have given a clear signal that we support changes to raise european standards of protection for young mothers. women are guaranteed a minimum period of maternity leave, which will henceforth be fully paid. the protection of the jobs of women returning to the labour market after a period of maternity leave has also been increased by preventing unjustified dismissals. the amendments introduced by the directive are a step in the right direction, guaranteeing women in europe a minimum level of maternity leave. i also welcome the encouragement to fathers to take care of their children by introducing two weeks of paternity leave.
in writing. − payments on time in commercial transactions are a priority for the proper functioning of european economies. unfortunately, the disparities in the respect of time limits in commercial transactions between member states are significant and it is therefore necessary to thoroughly review the current directive 2000/35/ec of 8 august 2002. the lack of transaction discipline is a very serious risk, especially for smes from countries already affected by the economic crisis. late payment often leads to disruptions in both the internal market and cross-border trade. in this context, i support the rapporteur's proposal to tighten the rules, introduce further instruments to protect businesses and make compulsory the compensation used to collect dues and interest when payments are not paid on time.
in writing. - current data show that poverty levels are rising in the european union. in many member states, poverty particularly affects children and the elderly, and the rise in short-term employment contracts and low, insecure incomes risks worsening living conditions for the whole of society. if you add to that the prevailing in some countries than the demographic, you get a recipe for a guaranteed economic collapse. our job is to ensure a decent life for all citizens. we cannot allow our children and grandchildren to suffer from hunger, unemployment and social exclusion. we must guarantee future generations adequate wages, job security, access to public services and social inclusion throughout their lives, from infancy to retirement.
in writing. − one of the most effective tools in the fight against poverty is to guarantee european union citizens a minimum income, including salaries, pensions and benefits. the minimum wage should be a universal law and not be a contribution. particular attention should be paid to social groups particularly at risk of poverty and social exclusion, including in particular persons with disabilities, large and disabled families, chronically ill persons and the elderly. the experience of some european union countries shows how important a role minimum incomes play in the fight against poverty and social exclusion, which is why i voted in favour of the ilda figueiredo report.
in writing. - poverty and social exclusion are manifestations of a lack of respect for human dignity. combating this phenomenon is a priority for the european union and is also enshrined in the millennium development goals. what can we do and what tasks can we take on? the most important thing is education and development, and that means solutions that teach people how they can overcome poverty by using their potential supported by systemic solutions. in short, to teach the know-how of the field. in developing countries, it is important to support infrastructure development, particularly access to water. development aid must be linked to the creation of conditions for the development of trade. the creation of growth and jobs is the best way to combat poverty in different regions of the world, rich and poor alike. the fight against poverty cannot be effectively fought by administrative regulations alone, even those that set a minimum income.
i fully agree with mrs anna gomes that human rights are one of the most important issues in our work and therefore i cannot understand what mrs lösing said, that money spent on human rights is sometimes or often misused. i don't understand that line. this is our constitutional, perhaps even our most important task as the european community. i would also like to refer to one of the instruments for promoting democracy and human rights in the world and to the statement that these instruments should be introduced and should operate independently of the consent of third countries and other public authorities. i think that's a very important sentence that shows our duty. sometimes we have to help build democracy and uphold human rights against the governments of some countries. i think it's worth doing, especially and above all where the right to freedom of expression is violated. it's our duty.
the european financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights is, in my view, an instrument that is being used and treated too technically at the moment. it should be more of a political tool of the european union, as it has a huge potential to support and promote democracy. however, this requires a change in approach to this european financial instrument. so far, the issue of promoting democracy has been overshadowed by human rights, which are of course incredibly important. but i think that the promotion of democracy itself, which is something else, should be elevated to a much higher level and given much greater importance. therefore, non-governmental institutions in countries with authoritarian governments should be strengthened. we need to build a grassroots democracy in these countries, from the bottom up. the focus should therefore be on civil society organisations that offer innovative ways to expand public space. to do this, firstly, regular monitoring of the performance of organisations that use european money should be introduced. the organisations themselves say that a forum should be set up to enable donors and beneficiaries to communicate, not only donors from the european union but also others, by means of regular meetings. the application forms should be simplified. right now, they're just not available to many. finally, the commission should seek to relax the financial regulation.
